# CHANGES.md
## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0026 — RGX-0078.5.d.4.i ARENA MODEL DECISION (SPEED PHASE, docs-only): candidate C CONFIRMED after a pre-code, tool-backed C-vs-B re-weigh — the Drop-correctness + durability deciders

Docs-only decision slice — NO code. Before writing a line of the phase's riskiest byte-identity change, a tool-backed scoping pass re-weighed the C-vs-B arena choice from session #99. The director delegated the call ("you are the expert coder — pick the SOTA, signoff, most durable, clean, rock-solid approach and roll"). Decision: **candidate C, on firmer Drop-aware footing** (zero drift from session #99).

- **Finding 1 — the type change is SINGLE-SITE (shrinks the surgery).** TOOL-VERIFIED the generated parsers `use crate::ast_pipeline::{… ParseContent, ParseNode, MemoEntry, …}` (`generated/regex_parser.rs:3`) — they do NOT define a private copy. So the type lives in exactly ONE place (`mod.rs`); the blueprint's "two copies in lockstep" worry is void. `ast_code_generator.rs` (its inert `quote!` template) is legacy/uninvoked — leave it alone.
- **Finding 2 — the crux the blueprint mislabeled "mechanical."** `ast_return_transform.rs` (the return-annotation codegen — the most byte-identity-fragile area: PGEN-RGX-0075/0077, the `<invalid_sequence_access>` sentinels) EMITS runtime code treating children as OWNED, MOVABLE values (~15 sites, `grep`-verified: `for node in nodes { array_elements.push(node) }`, `elements[N].content.clone()`, peel-`Alternative`-by-move, mid-transform `ParseNode { … }` construction). Under C these need read-then-push borrow discipline, not a blind `arena[id]` swap — concentrated risk in the fragile codegen.
- **Decider = Drop-correctness.** `ParseContent` carries `String` (`TransformedTerminal`) + `serde_json::Value` (`Json`) — heap-owning `Drop` types. Any arena MUST run their destructors or LEAK every parse (unbounded). **C (`Vec<ParseNode>` + `NodeId`)** is Drop-correct FOR FREE (the `Vec` drops each element) + single `'input` lifetime + no dep + folds `.5.d.3` memo-sharing. **Plain `bumpalo`** does NOT run `Drop` ⇒ leaks ✗ (disqualified; `bumpalo` is only transitively in `Cargo.lock:98`, not a direct pgen dep). A Drop-correct ref-arena (`typed-arena`) would add a dep AND a viral `'arena` lifetime.
- **Durability decider (the director's criterion).** `ParseContent`/`ParseNode` is a CORE type touched by 13 files; a viral `'arena` second lifetime is a permanent signature tax across all of them. **rust-analyzer** deliberately chose INDEX arenas (`la_arena::Idx`) over reference arenas for its syntax trees for exactly this reason — strong SOTA precedent that the single-lifetime index arena is the cleaner, more durable choice for a large tree-heavy codebase. The public boundary is already owned (`serde_json::Value`), so the arena is a purely internal detail either way.
- **⇒ candidate C.** Transform crux handled via read-then-push (resolve reads into owned locals / a `NodeId` list first, drop the `&arena` borrow, then push fresh wrapper nodes — non-overlapping borrows; fresh-node sites are rare, spread/flatten-spread only). Byte-identity gated CHEAPLY by the debug oracles (equivalence/combinator/semantic) before any fat-LTO. ⏭️ NEXT: execute the candidate-C code (migration order: `mod.rs` → interpreter mirror → codegen construction+regen → walkers → oracles → fat-LTO measure; land iff faster + byte-identical).

Files: `docs/tasks/RGX-0078.md` (`.5.d.4.i` ARENA MODEL DECISION section + checklist FIX line), `docs/book/src/inside-parser-performance.md` (the Drop-correctness + durability deciders narrated in lockstep), `MEMORY.md`, `CHANGES.md`. No code change. Status rows UNCHANGED (regex `Done`).

## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0020 — RGX-0078.5.d.4 R-d DESIGN (SPEED PHASE, docs-only): arena × `'input` lifetime ownership-model survey; candidate C recommended; BOTH pause points now surfaced for combined agreement

Docs-only design slice — NO code. Second `.5.d.4` design increment: designs **R-d** (the arena × `'input` lifetime ownership shape — the second pre-registered pause-and-agree point), so both R-a (session #98) and R-d are surfaced for the director's COMBINED agreement before any code, greenlighting the whole `.5.d.4` road as a unit (the tree's UNFORESEEN-ISSUE PROTOCOL + [[feedback_stick_to_agreed_plan_no_silent_drift]]).

- **Tool-grounded facts.** The two memo deep-clone sites R-d must eliminate: insert `ast_based_generator.rs:7185` (`result: Some(node.clone())`), hit `:7130` (`return Ok((node.clone(), …))`). The `'input` borrow constraint: `ParseContent::Terminal(&'input str)` — the tree borrows the input, which outlives the parse. **The decisive de-risker:** the public/crate boundary returns OWNED data (`parser_registry::parse_sample_ast_json*`→`serde_json::Value`, `embedding_api`→`Result<String,…>`), walked from the tree at the boundary via `ParseContent::to_json_value` — so `ParseNode<'input>` NEVER escapes borrowed ⇒ an arena is a purely INTERNAL detail (public API unchanged by construction; blast radius confined to internal machinery + the one boundary serialize walk). No arena crate is in `Cargo.toml` today.
- **Three ownership models weighed** (moves the 54.6% construction malloc? · `'input` coexistence · blast radius · new dep · folds `.5.d.3`?): **(A)** `Rc<ParseNode<'input>>` — single lifetime, cheap sharing, but still one heap alloc per node ⇒ does NOT move the 54.6% (predicted ~1% null alone, = standalone `.5.d.3`). **(B)** bump arena + `&'arena` two-lifetime `ParseNode<'input,'arena>` — moves the 54.6%, but needs `bumpalo` + a viral second lifetime through the internals. **(C ★ RECOMMENDED)** plain-`Vec` arena + `NodeId(u32)` indices — moves the 54.6% (bulk-alloc + mass-free) + folds `.5.d.3` memo sharing (memo→`NodeId`, hit is a `Copy`), keeps the SINGLE `'input` lifetime, NO new dep; price = threading the arena slice through the tree-walkers to resolve indices (mechanical, contained).
- **Recommendation: candidate C** — same performance envelope as B without the viral second lifetime or a new dependency; byte-identical by construction (structurally identical tree, referenced by index instead of `Box`/`Vec`; boundary JSON is the same bytes), proven by the `parse_harness_*` differential + PCRE2 diff + all-parsers regen. B is the fallback; A is retained only as the memo-sharing sub-step. **Sequencing:** R-d = increment (iii), NOT (i); the first code increment (i) (terminal-only lockstep for `atom`) needs no arena, so R-d is agreed IN PRINCIPLE now (greenlight direction C).

## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0019 — RGX-0078.5.d.4 DESIGN kickoff (SPEED PHASE, docs-only): director chose the lockstep road; R-a (furthest_position) RESOLVED + surfaced for agreement

Docs-only design slice — NO code. After RE-PROFILE #3 surfaced the re-sequencing options, the director chose **option A**: advance to `.5.d.4` (the lockstep DFA advance + arena), the ONLY lever that moves the dominant 54.6% construction malloc, folding `.5.d.3` (memo sharing) and `.5.d.2` (lazy winner-only materialization) in as composing pieces. Kicked off the `.5.d.4` design (docs-first; the code increment is gated on the R-a agreement, a pre-registered pause-and-agree point):

- **Machinery survey** (tool-grounded against `ast_based_generator.rs` `generate_or_logic`, the main/`.5.c.2` baseline): the multi-branch tournament is a SERIAL try-each — each branch tried from `parse_start` via `try_parse`, rolled back, winner by longest-match (`candidate_end > best_end`) with `@priority`/`@associativity` tie-break, then the winner's C3-B `SemanticRuntimeDelta` applied once. Cost = O(Σ branch-cost) with a full rollback per branch — the serial waste `.5.d.4` eliminates.
- **R-a (furthest_position) RESOLVED — the make-or-break correctness risk.** TOOL-VERIFIED: `furthest_position` is written at EXACTLY ONE site — rule-method entry (`ast_based_generator.rs:3288`; all **274** sites in `generated/regex_parser.rs` are that identical pattern; `match_string`/terminal matching never write it; the interpreter mirrors it at `parse_harness_interpreter.rs:851`), monotone, never rolled back. ⇒ the lockstep advance over terminal choice sites is **furthest-neutral by construction** (a terminal branch only bumps furthest to its entry = `parse_start`, already recorded — the exact `.5.c.2` soundness argument; group-family branches discriminate a deterministic introducer prefix `(?:`/`(?P<`/`(?=`/`(?!`/`(` then recurse via normal recursive-descent, preserving furthest there), with the `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` byte-level furthest check as the backstop. **Surfaced for the director's agreement before the first code increment.**
- **Capability gate** (parser-agnostic, CAPABILITY not grammar-name): DFA-discriminable choice sites (terminal / terminal-prefix-then-recurse); store-gated `@predicate` branches + non-prefix-disjoint recursive branches stay serial (byte-identical fallback per site). **R-d** (arena × `'input` lifetime) is the next design increment (its own pre-registered pause point). **Increment decomposition**: (i) terminal-only lockstep for `atom` (folds in lazy materialization) → (ii) group-family prefix discrimination → (iii) arena + memo sharing (the 54.6% lever) → (iv) generalize the gate; each independently measured + full ⛔ HARD-CONSTRAINT battery, land iff faster + byte-identical.

Files: `docs/tasks/RGX-0078.md` (`.5.d.4` leaf status + the `.5.d.4` DESIGN section), `docs/book/src/inside-parser-performance.md` (the decision + the R-a result narrated), `MEMORY.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md`. No code change. Status rows UNCHANGED (regex `Done`).

## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0018 — RGX-0078.5.d.3 RE-PROFILE #3 (SPEED PHASE, docs-only): the memo-subtree-sharing premise is FALSIFIED before building; re-sequencing decision surfaced to the director

Docs-only steering slice — NO code. Before building the high-risk `.5.d.3` (memo subtree sharing: `Rc`/arena handle × the `'input` lifetime), I applied the durable `.5.d.2` lesson ([[project_lazy_winner_only_materialization_lesson]]: *measure the marginal gain against the CURRENT baseline; don't infer*) + [[project_uvm_memory_not_the_memo]] ("profile, don't infer") + TOOLBOX-first, and profiled the memo-clone cost **specifically**. **`PGEN_REPORT_MEMO_STATS`** shows the memo footprint is tiny (largest pattern = 396 subtree-nodes across 218 entries = avg 1.8 nodes/entry, mostly non-allocating `Terminal(&str)` leaves). **macOS `sample`** (40 s @1 ms, 33,671 leaf samples, the eager/main `.5.c.2` baseline sha `449faa8b…`) puts the `.5.d.3` DIRECT target — `ParseNode::clone` (0.86%) + `ParseContent::clone` (0.41%) — at **1.27% of self-time**, the same speed-neutral territory as `.5.d.2`. The biggest *clone* in the profile is serde_json `Value::Object`/BTreeMap (the winner's return-annotation JSON transform, call-graph ancestry `to_json_value`), which `.5.d.3` does not touch. The real cost is **broad construction malloc — 54.6%** (malloc 24.4% / free 16.8% / memops 13.4%) — fixable only by the ARENA + construction-elimination, i.e. the `.5.d.4` lockstep advance, NOT standalone memo node-sharing.

**FINDING:** the `.5.d.3` premise ("memo deep-clones are the single biggest clone source") is **FALSIFIED**; standalone `.5.d.3` is a predicted ~1% null, and its value — like `.5.d.2`'s lazy materialization — is as a COMPOSING PIECE of `.5.d.4`. Two profile-indicated levers now stand out: the arena / `.5.d.4` lockstep (the agreed core; the only 54.6% lever, big + high-risk) and a NEW byte-identical low-risk detour — **precompiling the predicate expression** (parse the FIXED relational predicate to an AST once instead of re-splitting the string on every evaluation; `split_semantic_top_level` 2.8% + the `evaluate_relational_expression_inner` re-parse cascade; parser-agnostic). **⛔ The re-sequencing decision was SURFACED to the director (AskUserQuestion), NOT decided unilaterally** — per [[feedback_stick_to_agreed_plan_no_silent_drift]] (a queued leaf's premise falsified by a fresh profile changes the agreed next step: PAUSE → analyze → propose → AGREE, before acting). The agreed DESTINATION (the lockstep road to PCRE2 parity) is UNCHANGED. ## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0017 — RGX-0078.5.d.2 LAZY WINNER-ONLY MATERIALIZATION: built + proven byte-identical, then REVERTED (SPEED-NEUTRAL substitute for the already-landed first-set dispatch); the elegant tool + the lesson PRESERVED

`.5.d.2` implemented the lazy winner-only transform in the codegen (`ast_based_generator.rs` `generate_or_logic`): for a rule with no branch-phase `@predicate` (`rule_has_no_semantic_annotations` — the sound R-b capability gate), decide the tournament winner FIRST from cheap metadata (`should_take`, which never reads the transformed value) and run the return-annotation JSON-fold + `raw_content.clone()` ONLY for the winning candidate, BEFORE the position rollback (so `$text`/MatchedText still slices `input[parse_start..candidate_end]`, BRANCH-BROADCAST-FIX.3 preserved for free). Shared `should_take_selection` token keeps winner-selection identical across the eager/lazy paths. **Proven 100% byte-identical** — all 11 parsers regen'd; `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` (interp↔generated, seeds 0/7/42), combinator 27/27 (incl. `a|ab`), semantic 36/36, regex cert `fully_certified` UNKNOWN=0 spf `0/1/1`, `duality_hunt_gate` (no new sig), `regex_ast_shape_contract_gate`, source clippy, and a **PCRE2 fix-vs-nofix per-case diff EMPTY over 2188 cells** (`1878/310/262/48`).

**But SPEED-NEUTRAL, so REVERTED.** A decisive 7-round drift-controlled `regex_perf_probe` geomean-of-mins (both release fat-LTO binaries, distinct sha256, nofix regen confirmed eager) put fix ≈ **75.5 µs** vs nofix ≈ **75.9 µs** — heavy overlap, per-round sign flips, no decisive separation. **Root cause (director's framing):** first-set predictive dispatch (`.5.c.2`, the −75% lever) and lazy materialization are two DIFFERENT solutions to the SAME observable cost — the losing branches — so they are **SUBSTITUTES, not complements**. First-set removes a losing branch before it is tried; lazy removes its transform after; since first-set already deletes them, lazy has almost nothing left to defer. Per the SPEED-PHASE HARD CONSTRAINT (land iff faster + byte-identical) + the `.4.b`/`.4.c` precedent, a byte-identical NON-win does not land: the code was reverted (`git checkout` back to the `.5.c.2` baseline). **The tool + lesson are PRESERVED, not discarded** (director-requested): new decision record `docs/decisions/project_lazy_winner_only_materialization_lesson.md` (the elegant *parallel-not-sequential* materialization tool + the substitute-lever lesson), the `RGX-0078.5.d.2` leaf (full worked design), and a curated `inside-parser-performance.md` book note. Lazy materialization is **structurally required** by `.5.d.4` (a lockstep DFA advance cannot transform per-branch), so the tool returns there where it composes into a real win. **Next lever ⇒ `.5.d.3` MEMO SUBTREE SHARING** — the null proves the RE-PROFILE #2 ~70% clone/malloc is the memo deep-clones, not the transform. Files: `docs/decisions/project_lazy_winner_only_materialization_lesson.md` (new) + `INDEX.md`, `docs/tasks/RGX-0078.md`, `docs/book/src/inside-parser-performance.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md`. Code: reverted (no net source change). Status rows UNCHANGED (regex `Done`).

## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0016 — RGX-0078.5.d.1 DESIGN SPIKE (SPEED PHASE, docs-only): the lockstep simulation, decomposed into byte-identical increments (tool-backed by an engine-machinery survey)

Docs-only design spike (NO code) — the agreed `.5.d` first design (F5c/F5d), the "creative/inventive/out-of-the-box" road the director asked for, made concrete against the ACTUAL machinery. An engine-machinery survey (verified refs: `ast_based_generator.rs`, `semantic_runtime.rs`, `mod.rs`, `generated/regex_parser.rs`) produced two reframing findings: **(A1)** the tournament (`generate_or_logic`, `ast_based_generator.rs:3495`) is ALREADY half-lockstep — it attempts every branch from one shared baseline, captures each branch's semantic mutation as a `SemanticRuntimeDelta` (`extract_delta_since`, `:3925`), and applies ONLY the winner's delta once at the end (`apply_delta`, `:4096`) — that IS **F5d piece 2 (the COW store overlay), already shipped** (MEMO-STORE-SOUNDNESS.2). **(A2)** the RE-PROFILE #2 70% clone/malloc is now pinpointed and separable: the JSON-fold transform runs EAGERLY per branch attempt (`:3735`, "fold 24 keep 1") and the memo DEEP-CLONES the whole `ParseNode` on insert (`356691`) AND on every hit (`356658`).

**The creative decomposition** (every increment a piece of the agreed lockstep sim, NOT a standalone lever): `.5.d.2` **lazy winner-only materialization** (defer the transform from per-branch to winner-only — selection needs only `candidate_end`/priority, not the transform, so pick the winner from cheap `raw_content` then transform ONCE; byte-identical by construction, the `.5.b`/`.5.c` soundness family; the big quick win) → `.5.d.3` **memo subtree sharing** (replace the deep-clones with an `Rc`/arena handle) → `.5.d.4` **the lockstep DFA advance** (serial try-each → one forward scan, no backtracking; the store COW already there) → `.5.e` **GLL + true `(rule,start,end)` SPPF** (recursive/ambiguous, research-grade). The three F5c precisions (longest-match winner, lazy AST/effects, store-gated liveness) are preserved by every increment; the oracle per increment is the `parse_harness_*` byte-identical differential + the full ⛔ HARD-CONSTRAINT battery. Four open risks R-a..R-d (furthest_position preservation, predicate/transform coupling, effect ordering, `'input` lifetime × arena) are recorded as **pre-registered pause-and-agree points** per the director's UNFORESEEN-ISSUE PROTOCOL (pause → analyze → agree a solution together → proceed; no unilateral solve-and-drift). ## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0013 — RGX-0078.5.c.2 (SPEED PHASE): FIRST-SET PREDICTIVE DISPATCH LANDED — regex geomean −75% (~4× faster, ≈303µs→76µs), byte-identical

The biggest single RGX-0078 speed lever to date, and the payoff of the `.5.c.1` design spike. **Root cause** (`.5` profile): regex parse time is dominated by one rule — `atom`, a ~24-way `longest_match` branch tournament tried at every input character (`parse_atom` = 7565 profiler samples); under longest-match the engine evaluates EVERY alternative and keeps the longest, so at a plain literal char it still sets up, tries, and rolls back ~23 branches that cannot match — each paying a `try_parse` + `extract_delta` + a C3-B rollback-label `format!` (993 sites) + the per-attempt allocation. The profiled 59%-malloc and 6%-string buckets are the same defect seen twice: *"evaluate every branch, then discard most."*

**Fix** (codegen, parser-AGNOSTIC — every whitespace-sensitive grammar inherits it; NOT grammar-name-gated): new shared module `rust/src/ast_pipeline/first_set.rs` (the sound `FirstSetSummary` first-set analysis moved VERBATIM out of `annotation_validator.rs` — the four functions are pure, so the move is behavior-preserving and both the validator's ambiguity lints and codegen now share one algorithm), plus a FIRST-set prune guard in `generate_or_logic`. For a **rule-top-level `Or`** in a **terminal-whitespace-sensitive** grammar, each non-nullable + fully-resolved branch is wrapped in `if parse_start < input.len() && matches!(input.as_bytes()[parse_start], <first-bytes>) { … }` — skipping the entire branch body when the next input byte cannot begin any of the branch's FIRST terminals. Everything uncertain (nullable, `unresolved`, a regex token, `.`/lookahead/anchor, an unresolved ref) is ALWAYS tried, never pruned. Two soundness refinements derived tools-first before any code (recorded R1–R3 in the tree): **(R1)** top-level `Or` ONLY — `furthest_position` is bumped at rule ENTRY, so only there is `parse_start ≤ furthest` already ⇒ pruning is `furthest_position`-neutral by construction (a nested `Or` whose rule-ref branch would enter a child at `parse_start` could otherwise change furthest on reject → deferred to `.5.c.2.a`); **(R2)** gated on `layout_sensitivity().terminals` — the raw next-byte peek is sound only when no terminal layout-skip precedes the match (regex `@whitespace_sensitive: true` ⇒ **820 guards** emitted; every other grammar ⇒ **0 guards**, byte-identical source); **(R3)** an interior-mutable `grammar_tree` snapshot (`RefCell`, mirroring the existing `uses_match_regex: Cell`) avoids threading `grammar_tree` through 8 `generate_*` functions.

**Speed:** DECISIVE drift-controlled before→after ([[feedback_prove_independence_with_decisive_baseline]]) — BOTH release binaries fat-LTO (distinct sha256 `e2c28021…` with-fix vs `674c3ea4…` no-fix), measured **alternately** (`regex_perf_probe` 2000/200, geomean p50 over the 8 patterns, 3 rounds): NO-FIX `302,722 / 302,390 / 304,455 ns` → WITH-FIX `76,553 / 75,960 / 75,855 ns` = **−74.7% / −74.9% / −75.1%** (a ~4× speedup; ≈303µs → ≈76µs), clean separation, stable across rounds.

**Correctness byte-identical** (pruning is output-neutral BY CONSTRUCTION — a pruned branch would fail at char 1, contributing nothing to the longest_match winner, and does not lower `furthest_position` at a top-level `Or`): `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` GREEN (the interpreter, which has NO pruning, is byte-identical to the generated regex parser WITH 820 guards — verdict + typed AST + `furthest_position`, every registered grammar, seeds 0/7/42 — the strongest oracle for a too-tight first-set); `parse_harness_combinator_gate` GREEN (27/27 combinators + the `a|ab` longest-match discrimination); `parse_harness_semantic_gate` GREEN (36/36 store-gated constructs, diverge=0); regex certificate coverage `fully_certified` `UNKNOWN=0`, spf `0/1/1` at seeds 0/7/42 (== baseline); `regex_ast_shape_contract_gate` GREEN (aligned=4, drift=0); `duality_hunt_gate` GREEN (no new signature); **all 9 non-regex parsers regenerate BYTE-IDENTICAL** (json / systemverilog_preprocessor / scratch / rtl_const_expr / vhdl / rtl_frontend / return_annotation / semantic_annotation + systemverilog 69MB) — proving output-neutrality for every non-terminal-sensitive grammar; strict-source clippy exit 0 (changed files zero warnings); 58 `annotation_validator` unit tests pass (verbatim move behavior-preserving). This is the sound **first mile** of the fuller lockstep-simulation road (Thompson-NFA / RE2 / GLL); `.5.c` node done, follow-ons `.5.c.2.a` (nested-`Or` pruning) + `.5.d`/`.5.e` queued. ## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0009 — RGX-0078.5.c.1 (SPEED PHASE, docs-only): director-steered PIVOT to FIRST-SET PREDICTIVE DISPATCH + root-cause correction + design spike DONE

Director steer, this session: *"we let the parser blindly try every branch in the hope one succeeds — naive; works for accuracy, not speed."* Acting on it produced a **tool-backed root-cause correction** and a concrete, feasibility-proven design for the next `.5` lever.

**Root-cause correction (the `.5` re-profile mis-attributed the WHERE).** Starting `.5.b` (defer the `try_parse` Err arm's trace-only `caller_context` Strings), a tools-first audit of ALL `rollback_to_named` codegen emission sites + a grep of the CURRENT regex parser found the `try_parse` Err arm is only **2 sites** in `generated/regex_parser.rs`, while the SAME trace-only-`caller_context` root cause at the **C3-B per-branch tournament cleanup** (`ast_based_generator.rs:3873` `format!("{} (C3-B branch {}/{} cleanup)")`) is **993 sites**. The `.5` re-profile call-graph (`reprofile.txt`) confirms it: `RegexParser::parse_atom` = **7565 samples** (dominant leaf), with `alloc::fmt::format_inner` / `String::write_str` / `rollback_to_named` ALL its nested children — i.e. the profiled ≈6% string bucket is dominated by the tournament cleanup, NOT the 2 try_parse arms. So the `.5.b` fix as scoped is ≈null for regex; it was implemented (byte-identical by construction) then **REVERTED**. The 59% malloc + 6% string are BOTH symptoms of ONE root cause: **evaluate every branch, then discard most.**

**`.5.c` — first-set predictive dispatch (parser/EBNF-agnostic, chosen next lever).** Before a multi-branch tournament evaluates a branch, peek the next input char and SKIP (prune) any branch whose sound FIRST-set over-approximation cannot begin a match — eliminating the pruned branches' entire try / `extract_delta` / `format!` / `rollback` / malloc at the source. **BYTE-IDENTICAL by construction** (a pruned branch would fail at char 1 → contributes nothing to the `longest_match` winner). ⛔ **PRUNE, never PEG-commit**: committing by lookahead is sound ONLY when the survivor set is a singleton; ≥2 survivors still tournament (the longest_match winner depends on FULL match length, not the first char — `a|ab` on `"ab"`), per [[project_earlier_always_matches_unsound_backtracking]].

**Design spike `.5.c.1` DONE (F1–F4, tools-first, no code).** F1: a reusable, sound `FirstSetSummary { terminals, nullable, unresolved }` analysis already exists in `annotation_validator.rs` (`unresolved`=conservative "don't prune"; cycle/depth-guarded transitive refs). F2: codegen's tournament `generate_or_logic(alternatives: &[ASTNode])` iterates the SAME `ASTNode` type + threads the normalized `grammar_tree` ⇒ compute the guard from the exact branch node it guards → aligned BY CONSTRUCTION (reuse the ALGORITHM, not the raw-AST cached result). F3: regex `atom` = ~24 metachar-disjoint rule-ref branches (`.`/`[`/`(`/`\`…) ⇒ ~24→1-2 survivors on a plain literal char (large, sound win). F4: guard skips the whole branch body; `unresolved`/`nullable` branches emit NO guard (soundness); the equivalence/combinator/PCRE2 gates ARE the soundness oracle. Implementation is `.5.c.2` (next).

**Concurrency (director `fork/join_any` refinement) — right instinct, wrong grain for the inner Or-node.** Assessed + set aside with three converging tool-backed reasons: (1) granularity (ns branch-work vs µs thread-sync); (2) it MULTIPLIES the profiled 59% state-cloning malloc (N copies not 1); (3) `join_any` returns the first-to-FINISH = the SHORTEST match = the WRONG longest_match winner (parity break), and the deterministic `join_all` form waits for the slowest (no latency win); plus the Rust `&mut`/`Arc<Mutex>` ownership wall, and the parallel-parsing literature parallelizes INPUT REGIONS of large inputs, never one Or-node's branches. **Promoted to `.7`** at the correct grain: one-whole-parse-per-task batch `fork/join` + parse-cache (RGX/embedding-API side), the natural home for concurrency. Docs-only slice: `docs/tasks/RGX-0078.md` (`.5.b`/`.5.c`/`.5.c.1`/`.5.c.2`/`.7` nodes + F1–F4 + considered-parallelism blocks) + `MEMORY.md`. No code changed; repo returned clean before this commit. Status rows UNCHANGED.

## 2026-07-12 - PGEN-RGX-0078-0006 — RGX-0078.5.a (SPEED PHASE): first SOURCE/ENGINE lever LANDED — FxHash the per-rule annotation-table lookups, −5.4% geomean, correctness floor byte-identical

The first `.5` source/engine speed lever is committed — the build-flag phase (`.4`) is done, so this attacks the profiled cost directly. **Root cause** (`.2` profile, macOS `sample`, release): the SipHash/hashmap bucket = **6.0%** of regex parse self-time; the call-graph named the per-rule-entry lookup functions `has_rule` / `pre_predicates_for_rule` / `needs_raw_post_capture_for_rule` / `needs_raw_final_capture_for_rule`, all of which funnel through `directives_by_rule.get(rule_name)` / `.contains_key(rule_name)` — evaluated on **every rule entry and every backtrack** under the `longest_match` atom-tournament. The two tables were std `HashMap`, i.e. the default `RandomState` **SipHash** (a cryptographic, DoS-resistant, deliberately slow hash) — pointless for the grammar's own fixed rule-name keys. **Fix** (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/semantic_runtime.rs`, shared engine, parser-AGNOSTIC — every grammar's generated parser AND the interpreter share `CompiledSemanticRuntimeAnnotations`): switch `directives_by_rule` + `branch_directives_by_rule` to `rustc_hash::FxHashMap` (the Optim-#6 memo hasher). The public constructors (`from_parts` / `from_rule_directives`) keep taking `std::HashMap` and convert at the boundary (`.into_iter().collect()`, one-time O(rules) at construction), so the generated parser's emitted `from_parts(...)` / `set_fact_kinds(...)` calls are UNCHANGED — **NO codegen/regen**. `fact_kinds` / `predicate_defs` left std (not the profile-named hot path).

**Speed:** DECISIVE drift-controlled before→after ([[feedback_prove_independence_with_decisive_baseline]]) — built BOTH release binaries (fat-LTO, distinct sha256 `ff61ca80…` no-fix vs `674c3ea4…` with-fix) and measured them **alternately back-to-back** (`regex_perf_probe` 2000/200, geomean of noise-floor mins, 3 rounds): NO-FIX `323,050 / 318,777 / 317,913 ns` vs WITH-FIX `304,007 / 298,187 / 306,160 ns` = **≈ −5.4% geomean** (per-round −5.9% / −6.5% / −3.7%; ≈320µs → ≈303µs). Clean separation (worst with-fix 306,160 < best no-fix 317,913), every one of the 8 patterns improved in every round.

**Correctness floor — the ⛔ HARD constraint, every oracle green at its pre-optimization value.** Byte-identity is ARGUED by construction (the two maps are accessed EXCLUSIVELY by point lookup — `get`/`contains_key` — and only ever *counted* via `.keys()` in `len()`, never iterated for any output-affecting purpose, so a hasher swap cannot change output; FxHash's fixed seed is also strictly more deterministic than the std `RandomState`) and PROVEN by the re-run oracles: **PCRE2 compile-oracle** — decisive fix-vs-no-fix diff on the safe 2188-cell subset (80-deep-paren `line_4674` excluded up front) returns `1878/310/262/48` either way, per-case observations `diff` EMPTY → not one new false-accept/false-reject; **regex cert-coverage** (seeds 0/7/42) `total=267 witness=258 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true` spf `0/1/1` — identical to `.3`/`.4.a`; `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` / `parse_harness_semantic_gate` (36/36) / `duality_hunt_gate` (no new signature) / `regex_ast_shape_contract_gate` all GREEN; clippy strict-source exit 0 (the non-strict generated-parsers clippy pass shows only pre-existing generated-code debt, unchanged by this lib-only source change). Behavior-neutral internal perf change → no contract/schema/ledger bump. Lockstep: `RGX-0078.md` (`.5.a` leaf → done, `.5` frontier) + `inside-parser-performance.md` scoreboard (`.5.a` row + plain-terms paragraph + "levers ahead" #1) + `project_rgx_0078_regex_slowness_followup.md` + `LIVE_ACHIEVEMENT_STATUS` (tracker note; status rows UNCHANGED) + `MEMORY` + `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES`. A RELATIVE scan-substring capture reference of value zero — `(*scs:(+0)…)` / `(*scs:(-0)…)`, including leading-zero `(*scs:(+00))` / `(*scs:(-00))` — now REJECTs (`E_PARSE_FAILURE`; PCRE2 10.47 err 126 "a relative value of zero is not allowed"). Absolute `0`/`00` were already rejected (resolved index 0); every nonzero ref (`(*scs:(1))` `(*scs:(-1))` `(*scs:(+1))` `(*scs:(01))`) is unchanged. Fixed with ONE validator guard (`is_relative_reference && reference == 0`); the grammar is byte-unchanged.

**🧱 The numeric-migration WITNESSING WALL (surfaced to the director; `docs/decisions/project_scs_numeric_migration_witnessing_wall.md`).** The originally-planned `.4.7.b` — split `scs_capture_number` by sign so absolute gets `fact_count_at_least phase:final` and backward `-N` gets `phase:post`, shrinking the validator to `+N` — was BUILT and oracle-proven at the grammar layer, then REVERTED. cert-coverage (tools-first) exposed that sound scan-substring generation is **absolute-only**: the `@gen_predicate fact_count_at_least(regex_capture_group, $value)` compiles to a VALUE-DRAW `IndexUpTo` that whole-render-replaces `scs_capture_number` with an integer in `1..=prior_count` (empirically 0 signed scs refs in 60k stimuli). So the sign-split cannot keep BOTH `fully_certified` (with whole-render-replace the signed rules are never generated ⇒ `UNKNOWN=2`, measured) AND `spf=0` (with generation descent the forward `+N` branch renders unsound refs the validator rejects ⇒ spf spike — the [[project_gen_side_no_lacks_fact_branch_prune]] / `.4.8` A′ class). Forward `+N` is the exact blocked forward/suffix-count class of `.4.7.c` (the reach-driver cannot synthesize a trailing group). The migration also carries zero correctness value (the validator already handles absolute/backward correctly), so the whole numeric migration is ABSORBED into `.4.7.c` (to land as a unit when a forward/suffix-count primitive exists) and only the real bug is fixed at the current owner.

**Proven (re-runnable oracles).** `pcre2test` 10.47 (err 126, err 115 for absolute-0); full-pipeline confirmation that the released parser ACCEPTED `()(*scs:(+0)a)` / `()(*scs:(-0)a)()` before the fix (`parseability_probe`); new `rejects_scan_substring_relative_zero_capture_refs` (validator unit) + `regex_scan_substring_relative_zero_refs_reject_pcre2_faithfully` (full-pipeline registry pin, 5 rejects incl. mixed list + leading-zeros, 4 nonzero-accept guards, both profiles reject the zero forms). NO REGRESSION (grammar byte-unchanged): regex cert `total=267 witness=258 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true spf=0` seeds 0/7/42 (fully_certified PRESERVED — the wall avoided); the `.4.7.a` named test + all scs validator/registry tests green; `regex_parser_pgen_rgx_0086_embedding_version_consts_match_ledger` + `regex_parser_integration_contract_metadata_is_stable` green (consts↔ledger↔manifest = `1.1.104`/`1.1.106`); clippy source-strict exit 0. LOCKSTEP: embedding_api consts + JSON manifest + contract identity + "Release 1.1.104 / Contract 1.1.106 Highlights"; ledger `REGEX-0113`; regex book `changelog-index.md` + `compile-contract-validator.md` + HTML regen; top-book `parser-families.md`; decision note + INDEX; tree `.4.7.b`/`.4.7.c` + `TASK_TREE.md`; `LIVE_ACHIEVEMENT_STATUS.md`; `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md`; `MEMORY.md`.

## 2026-07-11 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0046 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.7.a: NAMED scan-substring capture references are now GRAMMAR-owned (behavior-neutral validator→grammar migration; 2nd consumer of the `phase: final` primitive)

NO release/contract/schema/ledger bump — surface- & conformance-NEUTRAL (the `.3.16`/`.3.17` precedent). A NAMED scan-substring capture reference `(*scs:(<name>))` / `(*scs:('name'))` must reference a capture name defined SOMEWHERE in the pattern (forward references legal); an undefined name REJECTs at parse completion (PCRE2 err 115). This was already rejected by the out-of-band `validate_scan_substring_capture_refs` (load-bearing); the check now lives in `grammars/regex.ebnf` as the **second consumer** of the `FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE` whole-input deferred-obligation primitive after `.4.11` — a `has_fact(regex_defined_capture_name, $name) phase: final` gate on `scs_capture_name`, checking the `.4.11` parse-side capture-name inventory. The pre-existing `@gen_predicate has_fact(regex_capture_name, $text)` is unchanged (`$text` = matched name, unaffected by the reshape) — generation stays duality-clean via the `.4.11` gen-source/parse-inventory two-fact split.

## 2026-07-11 - PGEN-FPP-0004 — FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE.3: close the multi-branch `view` footgun via an other-view resolver FALLBACK (tier-5 engine robustness, INERT on every shipped parser)

Engine-robustness slice completing the `FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE` tree (all three children now landed). No release/contract/schema/ledger bump — the change is byte-identical on every shipped parser. Closes the footgun the FIRST consumer (`REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.11`) surfaced and retires the per-consumer `view: shaped` workaround it had to use.

**The footgun.** A `@predicate` defaults to `view: raw`. On a MULTI-BRANCH (`Or`) rule the winning branch captures its raw `Sequence` as the final-predicate view, so a shaped-key `$ref`/`$name` (naming a `-> {…}` transform field) cannot resolve against the `Sequence` — the rule raises *"could not resolve attribute reference 'ref'"* and REJECTS even a DEFINED name. A single-branch rule resolved the same key only by the `semantic_raw_content == None` shaped-fallback ACCIDENT, which is why the `.2` single-branch isolation proof missed it. Root-caused tools-first in session #87 via `--trace-rules`.

**The fix (Option (b)-refined, director-authorized — a resolver fallback, NOT a default-flip).** Each argument resolver now computes `(selected_content, fallback_content)` from `spec.view` (the OTHER view is the fallback); a NAMED / object-key reference absent from the primary view falls back to the other content view BEFORE raising the unresolved-attribute error. Gated by a new shared `semantic_reference_is_named` helper mirroring `resolve_semantic_reference`'s named-vs-positional split — a positional `$N` walks the raw tree structurally and is NEVER retried against the other view (positional `$N` / `$text` semantics unchanged), and a key absent from BOTH views still errors (a real typo is never masked). Applies to ALL phases (pre/branch/post/final). Landed identically in the codegen-emitted resolver (`ast_based_generator.rs` `resolve_semantic_predicate_spec_against_content` + `try_…`, threaded through the value/try/properties resolvers) and its interpreter mirror (`parse_harness_interpreter.rs`). `@emit_fact` (an effect, not a predicate) passes its own single content as the inert fallback (byte-identical). `semantic_runtime.rs:3572` (`evaluate_content_aware_predicate`) needed NO change — it consumes `selected_content` only for `content_kind_is` (a content-KIND query, not a `$ref` resolution). Fix-hierarchy tier-5 (engine): the footgun is an engine-resolution inconsistency, not fixable below the engine except by the per-consumer `view: shaped` workaround this leaf retires.

**Proven (all re-runnable oracles, on the regenerated 11-parser set).** Scratch-slot isolation in a REAL generated parser: multi-branch default-view `has_fact(name_decl, $r) phase: final` → `k<a>decl a;` / `g<a>decl a;` (both branches) forward-ACCEPT, `k<a>decl b;` REJECT (obligation args resolved to `Identifier("a")` VIA the fallback). `parse_harness_semantic_gate` **36/36 CLEAN** — new MULTI-BRANCH default-view case `sem_final_multibranch_shaped_ref` byte-identical (interpreter == compile-and-run oracle) + 3 anchors; the 35 prior cases unchanged. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` over all **11** shipped parsers **regenerated with the new codegen** (INERT-ON-SHIPPED — regex's `.4.11` gates keep explicit `view: shaped`, resolve in-primary, never touch the fallback). `parse_harness_combinator_gate` 27/27. `duality_hunt_gate` pinned signatures unchanged. `regex_ast_shape_contract_gate` aligned=4 drift=0. Regex cert `--entry-rule regex --count 40` seeds 0/7/42 **UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true** (witness 258, spf 0/1/1 — byte-identical to the `.4.11` baseline). Named-ref spot-check `\k<aa>(?'aa'x)` / `(?&a)(?<a>x)` ACCEPT + `\k<zzz>` REJECT intact. Stage-1 source clippy exit 0. LOCKSTEP: book `semantic-store.md` (`view` note softened from "REQUIRED" to "optional self-documentation") + `parse-harness.md` (new row + 35→36) + `TOOLBOX.md` §1.8 (35→36) + decision record `.3 BUILD LANDED` anchor + tree + this file + `DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md` + `LIVE_ACHIEVEMENT_STATUS.md` + `MEMORY.md`.

## 2026-07-11 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0045 — REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.4.11: named-reference UNKNOWN-name reject is now GRAMMAR-owned (a genuine accepts-invalid correction — behavior-CHANGING; FIRST consumer of the `phase: final` primitive)

Regex release `1.1.102`→`1.1.103`, contract `1.1.104`→`1.1.105`, AST-dump schema `1`, ledger `REGEX-0098` Deferred→Fixed. A named reference to a group name defined NOWHERE in the pattern now **REJECTS** (PCRE2 err 115 "reference to non-existent subpattern") while a **legal forward reference** still **ACCEPTs** — closing a real released-parser accepts-invalid gap. All nine unknown-name spellings flip ACCEPT→REJECT: `\k<zzz>` / `\k'zzz'` / `\k{zzz}` (named backreferences), `(?P=zzz)` (Python), `\g{zzz}` (braced), `(?&zzz)` / `(?P>zzz)` / `\g<zzz>` / `\g'zzz'` (named subroutine calls); the controls `(?'aa'x)\k<aa>`, `\k<aa>(?'aa'x)` (forward), `(?<a>x)(?&a)`, `(?&a)(?<a>x)` (forward subroutine), `\g{a}(?<a>x)`, and every NUMERIC form (`(a)\1`, `(a)(b)\g<2>`, `(a)(?1)`) stay ACCEPT. Frozen acceptance spec = the `.3.22` oracle matrix, **17/17**.

**The FIRST consumer of the `FINAL-PHASE-PREDICATE` primitive.** Encoded purely in `grammars/regex.ebnf` (no engine/Rust logic change — only the release-version constants): (1) a two-kind fact split — `regex_defined_capture_name` (parse INVENTORY, `@emit_fact name=$name` on the shaped `named_group`/`python_named_group` rules) vs `regex_capture_name` (gen-draw SOURCE, `@gen_emit_fact` on the bare `capture_name`) — so the stimuli generator (which keys fact-draws on the producer rule's WHOLE RENDER) never splices a whole `(?<name>…)` group into a reference slot; (2) named forms peeled into HOMOGENEOUS rules so the whole-input gate binds to every named branch and never the numeric siblings — `named_backreference` (6 br), `named_subroutine_target` (2 br), a shared `reference_name` carrier, `braced_name_ref` removed; (3) `has_fact(regex_defined_capture_name, $ref|$name) phase: final, view: shaped` on the three named-reference gates.

**Root cause of the multi-branch bug (proven tools-first, `--trace-rules`).** The first build rejected even DEFINED names: a `@predicate` defaults to `view: raw`, and a multi-branch tournament captures the winner's raw `Sequence` for the final-predicate view — so a shaped-key `$ref` cannot resolve ("could not resolve attribute reference 'ref'") and the rule rejects. Single-branch rules only worked by the `semantic_raw_content=None` shaped-fallback accident (why the FPP.2 single-branch isolation proof missed it). Fix = `view: shaped` (fix-hierarchy level 1). A second bug (`\g<zzz>` accepting undefined) SELF-RESOLVED: once `named_backreference` no longer fails structurally, longest-match routes `\g<zzz>` to it over `simple_escape` — no `!"g"` guard needed. See `docs/decisions/project_final_phase_deferred_predicate_primitive.md` (FIRST-CONSUMER FINDING) + the book `phase: final` section (now documents the multi-branch `view: shaped` requirement).

**Conformance:** `.3.22` oracle matrix **17/17**; regex cert-coverage seeds 0/7/42 **UNKNOWN 2→0, `fully_certified=true`** (witness 256→258 — the named-ref rules are witnessable again); spf independence proven by a decisive clean-main baseline (clean-main **2/2/0** vs `.4.11` **0/1/1** — a NET improvement, so the residual pre-existing `\Q\E`/conditional generator spf is NOT a regression); `ast_shape_contract` regex **aligned=4 drift=0** (inventory 236→238 re-synced; accepted-AST byte-identical — `view` is a predicate, not a return-shape); `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` regex byte-identical (the interpreter mirror honors `view: shaped`); `duality_hunt_gate` pass; `regex_pcre2_compile_oracle_gate` recorded in ledger `REGEX-0098`.
