## 2026-07-08 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0014 (REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3.16): the numeric-callout [0, 255] bound grammar-encoded STRUCTURALLY — the declared `@range` design refuted tools-first, `find_invalid_numeric_callout` deleted (5th contract migration), NO version bump

Session #64. Released-parser slice, conformance- & surface-NEUTRAL (no release/contract/schema/
ledger change — release stays 1.1.84 / contract 1.1.86 / schema 1).

- **Issue (the `(?C262)` duality class, EVIDENCED `-0015`):** PCRE2 rejects a numeric callout whose
  VALUE exceeds 255 (err 138; leading zeros accepted — `(?C0255)` compiles, `pcre2test` 10.47) but the
  bound lived OUT-OF-BAND in `find_invalid_numeric_callout`, invisible to generation: 5/60 generated
  callout samples were parser-rejected (`(?C4135)` …).
- **Design adjudication (tools-first):** the leaf's declared `@range: [0, 255]` design was REFUTED
  before implementation — the SC-08 machinery is ATOM-scoped on BOTH sides (parse guards spliced only
  after literal/regex atom matches; generation sampling only in `generate_regex_sample`), and the
  self-hosted regex grammar has no atom spanning a multi-digit number: a mini-grammar generation probe
  with `@range` on a native `digits` body emitted `7562`/`3245`/`0935`/… — inert, and deleting the
  validator under it would have opened an accepts-invalid hole. A second probed hazard: Or-rooted
  rules get NO rule-level `@transform` span fallback (emitted-parser greps) → the wrapper shape.
  **Consequence recorded for `.3.21`:** the LIMIT `=value` u32-range leaf is the same class and cannot
  use `@range` as-is either.
- **Fix (grammar tier, structural):** `callout_arg = callout_number | callout_string`;
  `@transform`-span `callout_number = callout_number_body`; `callout_number_body = "0"+
  callout_number_core? | callout_number_core`; `callout_number_core` = the 5-branch nonzero-led ≤255
  encode. Out-of-range runs have no fully-consuming parse; generation is in-range BY CONSTRUCTION.
  Validator fn + call + 2 unit tests DELETED; new full-stack pin
  `regex_numeric_callout_range_rejects_at_the_grammar_layer_pcre2_faithfully` (10 rejects / 19
  accepts / typed-int AST / both profiles).

  spf=0); lint 0/0 (220 rules); svpp 74/74/0 ×3; PCRE2 oracle gate byte-identical baseline
  (1857/46/292/338); broader corpus 0 fails; differential-equivalence gate 4/4 (regex stays

## 2026-07-08 - PGEN-REGEX-PCRE2-0013 (REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3.15): character-class member VISIBILITY & the PCRE2 class-open model reject/accept PCRE2-faithfully — REGEX-0091 fixed, the checks grammar-encoded, regex release 1.1.84

Session #62. RELEASED regex slice (release `1.1.83`→`1.1.84`, contract `1.1.85`→`1.1.86`,
AST-dump schema stays `1`, ledger `REGEX-0091`).

- **Issue (rejects-valid, 17 flips + 3 wrong ASTs):** PGEN rejected `[\E]x]` (PCRE2: the stray
  `\E` is invisible, the first `]` is a LITERAL member — the class `]x`), `[^^]` (a caret after
  the negation is an ordinary member), `[\E^]x]` (the negation caret is recognized THROUGH
  invisibles), and 14 sibling spellings — all `pcre2test` 10.47-ACCEPTED; and it accepted
  `[\E^a]`-family patterns with a PCRE2-unfaithful NON-negated AST. The generator emitted
  invisible-only classes (`[\E]`) the validator rejected — the standing duality-break signature.
- **Root cause:** class non-emptiness counted PCRE2-INVISIBLE items at the grammar
  (`class_body_nonempty = class_item+`), `\Q`/`\E` leaked through the class-escape `any_char`
  catch-alls, and the validator's `scan_char_class` modeled the class opening as
  immediate-position checks (initial-`]` only directly after `[`; unconditional error on
  `]`-with-no-substantive-item; a silent `^`-skip instead of negation semantics).
- **Fix (grammar tier; 4th compile-contract migration):** the full PCRE2 class-open model in
  `grammars/regex.ebnf` (3-alt `char_class`, `class_negated_open` negation-through-invisibles,
  visibility-led non-empty bodies with `-> [$1*, $2, $3*]` flat-list byte-parity, structural
  nocaret first-visible slot, `!"Q"`/`!"E"` guards both profiles); validator class-open paths
  deleted, scanner aligned via `skip_invisible_class_items`.
- **Verified:** exactly the 17 flips over the 84-cell oracle matrix (both profiles), zero
  collateral; still-accepted ASTs byte-identical except the 3 documented negation corrections;
  cert `217/217 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified spf=0` ×3 seeds; lint 0/0; suites 880/838/761;
  equivalence/dual-run/oracle/broader-corpus/svpp/book gates green; hunter re-run: the `[\E]`
  signature GONE (1/1/2 → 1/0/0 per 100).
- **Lockstep:** ledger row + embedding consts + contract JSON/md (Identity + 1.1.84/1.1.86
  Highlights); regex book (changelog, `rules-char-class.md` rewritten to the current typed truth,
  class-open examples, json-carrier inventory, HTML); top book (parser-families handoff,
  stimuli-and-quality closure note); shape-contract manifest inventory 196→202; task tree + index.

  4/5/4 unique breaks, deterministic — same class set as `.4.4`.
- **Root cause (WHY+WHERE, tool-backed, per class):** every shrunk reproducer fed to the REAL
  parser fails with the post-parse-CONTRACT message, not a grammar backtrack — the grammar
  structurally ACCEPTS all 6 forms; the generator is contract-BLIND (grep-verified: zero
  references to `regex_compile_validation`/`post_parse_semantic_contract` in
  `stimuli_generator.rs`); the contract runs UNCONDITIONALLY in both profiles
  (`parser_registry.rs:394/:407/:1226`). Each class's grammar site + validator site + PCRE2
  10.47 oracle verdict are pinned in the design §2 table. All 6 classes are exactly
  not-yet-encoded rows (5/6/7/8/9) of the `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3` validator-migration table —
  the duality break exists BECAUSE those checks live out-of-band of the EBNF.
- **🔎 NEW FINDING (a real accepts-invalid divergence in the RELEASED regex parser):** PGEN
  accepts all 7 quantified escape-anchors `\A*` `\b*` `\B?` `\G+` `\z*` `\Z*` `\K*` that PCRE2
  10.47 rejects (err 109) — `find_invalid_quantified_anchor` covers only `^`/`$`; latent because
  the oracle corpus lacks the forms (POSIX aliases `[[:<:]]*`/`[[:>:]]+` are parity-accepted).
  Routed to `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3.13`, which owns the row-8 structural encoding that fixes the
  duality class AND the divergence in one slice.
- **Design decisions:** encodings are PLAIN (no profile split — the contract rejects in both
  profiles today, so verdict parity everywhere); each encoding slice removes its matching
  validator branch same-slice (the `.3.2` precedent) with `pcre2test` + oracle-gate parity proof.
  scs (class 6) parse-time predicate proven UNSOUND — forward references are LEGAL
  (`(*scs:('a'))(?<a>x)` oracle-accepted) — so its fix is generation-side store-aware
  (`STIMULI-SIGNOFF.13.4` + `REGEX-PCRE2-FIDELITY.3.17`). The `(?C262)` `@range` route is
  BLOCKED on the interpreter's missing value-constraint mirror (`STIMULI-SIGNOFF.13.2` lands the
  parser-agnostic mirror first — a latent platform hole for ANY grammar adopting `@range`).
- **Cert-spf adjudication (the leaf's second mandate) DECIDED:** the cert config stays (its

## 2026-07-07 - PGEN-BOUNDED-QUANT-0001 (BOUNDED-QUANT.1): bounded quantifiers `{n}`/`{n,m}`/`{n,}`/`{,m}` compile end-to-end — the codegen half-wire (PARSE-HARNESS.6.1 finding #1) is CLOSED

Session #53. **Parser-agnostic engine-helper fix + per-combinator proof.** The four bounded
quantifier forms are declared in `grammars/ebnf.ebnf` (164-186) and documented in the ebnf parser
book as first-class — but parser codegen hard-aborted on all of them, while the stimuli generator
happily generated strings for the same grammar: a live generator⟷parser duality break (the
EBNF-single-source-of-truth defect class) plus a user-facing book drift.

- **Reproduced live (tools-first):** `ast_pipeline bounded_quant.ebnf --generate-parser` →
  `Error: Failed to generate parser using AST-based generator` / `Unknown quantifier: 2,3`;
  the SAME grammar under `--generate-stimuli --count 5 --seed 0` → correct 2..3 repetitions,
  `sample_successes=5/5`.
- **Root cause (WHY+WHERE):** a dialect split on the `Quantified::quantifier` surface string.
  The Rust EBNF frontend emits the brace-STRIPPED raw-AST token — `item{2,3}` →
  `["quantifier","2,3"]` (`parse_braced_quantifier`, `rust/src/ebnf_frontend.rs:1013-1032`;
  contract-locked by `tokenizes_regex_and_bounded_quantifier`). The canonical Layer-0 decoder
  `parse_quantifier_bounds` (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs:925`) decoded only `?`/`*`/`+` and the
  BRACED spellings → `None` → both codegens abort (`ast_based_generator.rs:4013-4015`,
  `ast_code_generator.rs:437-439`); the interpreter (`parse_harness_interpreter.rs:2073`) and 7
  `grammar_wellformedness.rs` sites silently misread bounded forms via their `unwrap_or`
  fallbacks. The stimuli generator diverged because it bypassed the canonical helper through a
  private, duplicated brace-less bounds parser (`stimuli_generator.rs:10346`) — duplicated logic
  drifting exactly as the duplicate-metadata doctrine predicts.
- **Fix (one clean change, no menu):** the canonical `parse_quantifier_bounds` now normalizes
  `{…}`-wrapped input and decodes BOTH spellings through one inner parser (braced acceptance
  unchanged; `+6` unit tests incl. both-spelling invalid-form rejection). The stimuli generator's
  private decoder is DELEGATED to the canonical helper (unbounded maxima still clamp to
  `config.max_repeat`, never below `min`) — one decoder, drift impossible. The frontend-emission
  alternative was rejected: the brace-less token is a pinned cross-frontend raw-AST contract.
- **Per-combinator proof:** `parse_harness_combinator_suite` grew four `Combinator` variants +
  isolating cases — `quant_bounded_exact` (`item{2}`), `quant_bounded_range` (`item{2,3}`),
  `quant_bounded_at_least` (`item{2,}`), `quant_bounded_at_most` (`item{,2}`) — each proving the
  exact accept window byte-identically (verdict + `furthest_position` + typed AST) on the
  interpreter AND the compile-and-run oracle (the real codegen): 16 → **20 cases**.
- **Verified:** reproducer `--generate-parser` abort → parser generated (129 KB); stimuli output
  byte-identical pre/post delegation; `parse_harness_combinator_gate` **20/20 CLEAN** (2 gate
  tests); `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` **4/4** (11 CERTIFIED grammars byte-identical);
  `parse_harness_semantic_gate` **2/2** (24/24); features-on lib **811 passed / 0 failed**;
  emit-neutrality PROVEN — `make focus_json` + `make focus_regex` regen `cmp` byte-identical, and
  a raw-AST scan of all 15 frontend-parseable shipped grammars found ZERO bounded-quantifier
  tokens (the 3 `*_lrm_extracted.ebnf` snapshots are frontend-unparseable raw artifacts,
  pre-existing); clippy strict-source GREEN; `mdbook_docs_gate` + `ebnf_parser_book_gate` GREEN.
- **Lockstep:** TOOLBOX §1.7 (bounded forms now covered; honest bound narrowed to direct-LR);
  top book *The Parse Harness* (20-case table + the closure story); ebnf parser book
  `quantifiers.md` — its "all seven forms are first-class" claim is now TRUE, and its false

  inside regex LITERALS, not EBNF quantifiers); `docs/tasks/PARSE-HARNESS.md` §20 LIVE-SPEC note;
  NEW tree `docs/tasks/BOUNDED-QUANT.md` (full acceptance checklist).

## 2026-07-07 - PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0152 (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.A2.4): `DuplicateAlternative` verdict + `DuplicateOf` certificate made SELECTION-SEMANTICS-AWARE — the A2.2/A2.3/A2.4 "PEG commits" arc is COMPLETE

Session #52. **The LAST unconditioned ordered-choice deadness verdict.** The linter's
`DuplicateAlternative` shadowing verdict ("two identical alternatives — the later is unreachable")
carried the same latent assumption A2.2/A2.3 retired: it assumed the earlier twin always wins. But
PGEN's `|` is a branch TOURNAMENT — equal-length twins tie, and the winner is decided by `@priority`
(compared first) then `@associativity` (`left`→earlier, `right`→later, `nonassoc`→the tie fails the
whole choice), all under a `@deterministic_group` evaluation-order rotation.

- **Tool-backed root cause (Protocol D, scratch slot, `scratch := "a" | "a"`, input `a`).** Four
  live probes read from the engine's own `🏁 selected branch N/M` trace / accept-reject verdict:
  **(R)** `@associativity: right` → `🏁 selected branch 2/2 (… associativity=right)`; **(P)**
  `@priority: [0, 5]` → `🏁 selected branch 2/2 (priority=5)`; **(D)** `@deterministic_group:
  "spin"` → `🏁 selected branch 2/2` (rotation makes the later twin the incumbent a `left` tie
  keeps); **(N)** `@associativity: nonassoc` → both twins REJECT `a` while the deduplicated control
  `probe_n_single := "a"` ACCEPTS it (the nonassoc tie fails the whole choice). In R/P/D the engine
  SELECTS the branch the linter branded dead; in N the "merge or remove" advice would change
  acceptance.
- **Fix (linter tier — ZERO parse-behavior change, byte-identical regen).** New
  `RuleSelectionSemantics::duplicate_verdict` conditions the verdict on the rule's effective
  `@associativity`/`@priority`/`@deterministic_group`/branch-predicate surface, and the `DuplicateOf`
  proof certificate re-derives the same condition. New reason `DuplicateAlternativeNonassocTie` for
  the tie sub-case ("restructure deliberately," since removing one duplicate changes acceptance).
  The selection semantics are resolved by NEW shared `effective_rule_associativity` /
  `effective_rule_branch_priorities` / `effective_rule_deterministic_partition_policy` (plus the
  moved-shared `SemanticDeterminismPartitionPolicy`) in `semantic_directive_registry.rs` — the SAME
  functions codegen's tournament now DELEGATES to (single source of truth; the two can never drift).
  A2.4-D also tightened the A2.3 fixed-prefix verdict to require no partition rotation (rotation
  reorders `ordered` first-success). 3 source files; no new grammar constructs; no parser regen.
- **Verified.** ADDRESSED: R/P/D probes rc=1→rc=0; N keeps rc=1 with the new truthful tie message;
  defaults `"a"|"a"` and `@branch_policy: ordered` keep rc=1 (sound sub-cases). NO-REGRESSION:
  lib **695/695** (+3 A2.4 tests, wellformedness module 48/48); shipped-grammar shadowing sweep
  unchanged (12 shipped at 0; `systemverilog_lrm_profiled_generated` at 23 — grep-proven zero
  conditioning annotations, identical default path); byte-identical regen of ALL 4 policy-carrying
  grammars proving the codegen delegation emit-identical — `json` (defaults), `rtl_frontend`
  (`priority_first`×16), `systemverilog` (`@priority`×4), `regex` (`@precedence`×4), `cmp` clean each;
  `parse_harness_combinator_gate` **2/2**; `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` **GREEN** (canonical
  UNKNOWN=12, union UNKNOWN=1, residual `context_member_method_call`, deterministic seeds 0/7/42);
  clippy source-strict (generated-stage `eq_op` debt pre-existing + byte-identical); `mdbook_docs_gate`
  green.
- **Lockstep (same commit).** Top book *Grammar Well-Formedness* chapter (A2.4 paragraph + updated
  "gating shadow forms" conclusion); `TOOLBOX.md` §5.1 + Protocol D precedent list; decision record
  `docs/decisions/project_duplicate_alternative_selection_semantics_conditional.md`; auto-memory
  `project_earlier_always_matches_unsound_backtracking` (arc marked COMPLETE). **NO release bump.**

With A2.2 (always-succeeds retired), A2.3 (fixed-prefix policy-conditioned), and A2.4 (duplicate
selection-semantics-conditioned), **every surviving ordered-choice deadness verdict now names AND
checks the selection semantics it assumes** — the certifying-linter "never declares a live fragment

## 2026-07-06 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0014 (PARSE-HARNESS.6.1): structural combinator isolating suite — the interpreter is byte-identical to the compile-and-run oracle PER structural combinator (16/16 CLEAN)

Session #46. **CODE leaf — test-only tooling, parser-AGNOSTIC, NO engine / grammar / codegen / generated-parser change (no `generated/*` regenerated): adds `rust/src/parse_harness_combinator_suite.rs`, wires `pub mod parse_harness_combinator_suite;` in `rust/src/lib.rs` (`#[cfg(feature = "ebnf_dual_run")]`), adds the `parse_harness_combinator_gate` Makefile target.** Extends the proven `.4` smoke-set pattern into a systematic, gated per-combinator suite — the coverage that upgrades the interpreter's trust from "the shipped grammars' constructs" (the `.5` gate) to "any grammar built from PGEN's structural constructs."

- **Reproduced (BEFORE):** the `.5` differential-equivalence gate certifies the interpreter byte-identical only over constructs the *shipped* grammars use (§3.3). No per-combinator isolation existed — so the interpreter's trust on an ARBITRARY grammar (the harness's whole point, e.g. A2.3's `a | ab`) was not established construct-by-construct.
- **Root cause (WHY + WHERE, tools-first — a capability build, so the evidence is the empirical grounding via the real oracle, measure-then-lock):** every isolating grammar was validated to compile through `ast_pipeline --generate-parser` before use, and the differential measurement established the true oracle verdicts. That loop **tool-established three facts** (each caught by the oracle, not guessed):
  1. **bounded quantifiers `{N}`/`{N,M}`/`{N,}`/`{,M}` are half-wired** — the EBNF frontend parses `item{2}` into a `["quantifier","2"]` node and the shared runtime `parse_quantifier_bounds` honors the bounds, but **codegen aborts with `Unknown quantifier: 2`** (no handler in `generate_quantified_logic`), so the compile-and-run oracle cannot build them → `?`/`*`/`+` are the covered forms;
  2. **LR-elimination prepends the `_lr_base`/`_lr_suffix` helpers to `rule_order`**, so `rule_order[0]` is no longer the semantic entry (`expr`) — the LR case names the entry explicitly, applied identically to both sides;
  3. **bare DIRECT left-recursion `A := A x | y` is NOT structurally eliminated** — PGEN's `detect_left_recursive_chain_plan`/`extract_rule_reference_name` (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs`) match only the **wrapper/indirect** form (a multi-element sequence alt is not a bare rule-ref), so direct LR is left to runtime cycle-breaking (`RecursionGuard`), where interp & oracle diverge on `furthest_position` (interp 2/4 vs oracle 0; verdicts agree) — a KNOWN out-of-scope interpreter-fidelity gap.

Measurement map: `16/16 combinator cases CLEAN`.
- **No regression:** purely additive test-only tooling; NEVER invoked by any parse/codegen/cert path; `git status` = only `rust/src/parse_harness_combinator_suite.rs` (new) + `rust/src/lib.rs` + `rust/Makefile` (+ docs) — **no `generated/*_parser.rs` regenerated** → the 11 CERTIFIED grammars + SV byte-identical by construction. ## 2026-07-06 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0012 (PARSE-HARNESS.5.5): rtl_const_expr corpus — a curated-input corpus for the un-generatable precedence cascade promotes `rtl_const_expr` DEFERRED→CERTIFIED (11th grammar; DEFERRED now empty)

This is a **corpus fix, not a fidelity fix** — the leaf's thesis, now VERIFIED.

- **Reproduced (BEFORE):** `PGEN_PHEQ_ONLY=rtl_const_expr …::measurement` (default ladder [6,12,18], seeds 0/7/42) → `rtl_const_expr DIVERGE samples=0 agree=0 diverge=0`. Zero corpus, so honestly DEFERRED (samples_total==0 ⇒ not clean).
- **Root cause (WHY + WHERE, tools-first):** the stimuli generator cannot supply a usable corpus for `rtl_const_expr`. Tool-established via the CLI generation sweep (`ast_pipeline grammars/rtl_const_expr.ebnf --generate-stimuli --count 8 --seed 0 --max-depth D`, debug binary rebuilt with `ebnf_dual_run`): depths **6/12/16/18/20/24/28 → FAIL** (`Error: Stimuli generation depth exceeded max_depth=N while expanding rule 'multiplicative_expr'` / `'identifier'`), depth **32 → succeeds but only pathologically huge** expressions (thousands of chars), depths **40/60/80 → HANG** (25 s timeout; the super-linear pathology). WHY: the grammar's expression core is a **~16-level precedence cascade** (`rtl_const_expr → conditional_expr → … → multiplicative_expr → unary_expr → primary_expr → literal → decimal_integer`, `grammars/rtl_const_expr.ebnf:11-74`), each level `X := Y (op Y)*` — so the generator needs `max_depth ≳ 30` just to reach a leaf, and by then the ten `(op Y)*` quantifiers each re-descend the whole chain (super-linear). WHERE: the corpus was generation-only in `build_corpus` (returns `[]` for this grammar). A CORPUS-CONSTRUCTION gap, not an interpreter fidelity bug.
- **Fix (fix-hierarchy tier = new tooling / plumbing):** a general parser-agnostic curated-input-corpus mechanism (`CURATED_CORPUS: &[(&str, &[&str])]`, keyed by grammar name, next to CERTIFIED/DEFERRED/EXCLUDED) + `build_corpus` appending curated inputs (deduped, with the same truncation reject-path probes as generated samples), seeded with a construct-complete `rtl_const_expr` list. The differential compares the interpreter against the **authoritative generated parser**, so curated INPUTS carry no expected-output "mirror" risk (the oracle supplies the verdict + AST). Then `rtl_const_expr` promoted DEFERRED→CERTIFIED.
- **Addressed (AFTER, re-runnable oracles):** measurement `rtl_const_expr DIVERGE samples=0` → **`CLEAN samples=151 agree=151 diverge=0`**; `make -C rust parse_harness_equivalence_gate` → **4 passed** (`certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` now includes `rtl_const_expr`; ratchet forced the promotion; completeness holds; comment-arm matrix unaffected). Grounding cross-check: `rtl_const_expr` cert-coverage still fully certifies at its tuned `--max-depth 32` window (`total=48 witness=48 UNKNOWN=0 fully_certified=true`).
- **No regression:** purely additive test-only tooling; `git status` = only `rust/src/parse_harness_equivalence.rs` + docs — **no `generated/*` regenerated** → the 10 previously-certified grammars + SV byte-identical by construction, and the gate re-proves them directly (SV sv_2017 included in `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical`). Clippy-clean in the module; `mdbook_docs_gate` GREEN.
- **Novel / latent (surfaced to director):** the stimuli generator has a **known-but-now-sharply-characterized weakness on deep left-precedence-cascade grammars** — a whole class (any expression grammar with N precedence levels each wrapping `(op X)*`). rtl_const_expr is only *unbiased-generatable* in a razor-thin depth-32 window; general shallow/deep configs fail or hang. A natural capability-gap item for the stimuli-generator signoff vision (`project_stimuli_generator_signoff_vision`) — e.g. precedence-cascade-aware or iterative-deepening/memoized generation. ## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0011 (PARSE-HARNESS.5.3): return_annotation fidelity — canonicalizing the LR-chain `wrapper_specs` blob promotes `return_annotation` DEFERRED→CERTIFIED (10th grammar)

Session #44. **CODE leaf — a SHARED codegen serialization primitive, parser-AGNOSTIC, and the FIRST `.5.x` leaf to touch codegen (all prior were interpreter-only): edits `rust/src/ast_pipeline/unified_return_ast.rs` (a `#[serde(serialize_with)]` SORTED serializer on `UnifiedReturnAST::Object.properties`), `rust/src/parse_harness_equivalence.rs` (promote `return_annotation` DEFERRED→CERTIFIED + a NEW `probe_return_annotation_divergence` byte-level scout); regenerates `generated/return_annotation_parser.rs` + `generated/semantic_annotation_parser.rs` (the ONLY two grammars with Object-template `wrapper_specs`); NO engine / grammar change; SV untouched (release `1.0.167` / schema `16` unchanged).** Closes the interpreter's return_annotation divergence, taking the differential-equivalence gate from **9 → 10 CERTIFIED** grammars.

- **Reproduced (BEFORE):** `PGEN_PHEQ_ONLY=return_annotation …::measurement` (ladder [6,12,18], seeds 0/7/42) → `return_annotation DIVERGE samples=68 agree=50 diverge=8 (+10 suppressed)`. All 8 are `[Ast]` (both ACCEPT, same-length AST, different bytes); every diverging sample is a dotted property-access (`$1.S15`) or array-access (`$1[$1*]**`) — an LR-eliminated rule.
- **Root cause (WHY+WHERE — TOOLS-FIRST, and it REFUTED the scouting log's hypothesis; full detail `docs/tasks/PARSE-HARNESS.md` §18):** the scouting log had guessed an Object KEY-ORDER divergence the interpreter should "mirror from codegen." The new `probe_return_annotation_divergence` scout dumped both exact `wrapper_specs` blobs and showed there is NO stable codegen order to mirror: the interpreter picks a DIFFERENT Object key order for the SAME rule across samples **in one run** (`$1.S15`→`{property,base,…}`, `$1[$1*]**`→`{type,…}`, `$1.S15K.vbn**`→`{property,type,…}`) — the fingerprint of std `HashMap` non-determinism. WHERE: the `_pgen_lr_chain` `wrapper_specs` blob is `serde_json::to_string(&wrapper_specs)` at `rust/src/ast_pipeline/mod.rs:1943` (LR-elimination), where each `annotation_template` is a `UnifiedReturnAST::Object { properties: HashMap }` (`unified_return_ast.rs:56-58`). Codegen FROZE one arbitrary HashMap order into `generated/return_annotation_parser.rs:11473`; the interpreter re-serialized a fresh (itself non-deterministic) order each `load_gen_ast`. So the two blobs are independent, non-canonical HashMap serializations of the same semantically-orderless content — nothing to mirror. Tool trail: gen-AST blob ≠ frozen literal ≠ runtime output = three different orders; the oracle stable only because frozen, the interpreter not.
- **Fix (fix-hierarchy tier = shared codegen serialization primitive — the lowest tier that CAN fix it; an interpreter-only fix is impossible when the oracle's own order is a non-canonical frozen artifact):** a `#[serde(serialize_with = "serialize_properties_sorted")]` on `UnifiedReturnAST::Object.properties` emits keys in SORTED order at EVERY serialization site at once (the LR-elim gen-AST blob, codegen's frozen literal, and the interpreter's in-process re-serialization) → all sorted → byte-identical. Parser-agnostic (a shared type used by every grammar); deserialization unchanged (still into a `HashMap`; key order is semantically irrelevant). Then promoted `return_annotation` DEFERRED→CERTIFIED in `parse_harness_equivalence.rs`.
- **Addressed (verified — re-runnable oracles):** `PGEN_PHEQ_ONLY=return_annotation …::measurement` `DIVERGE 8` → **`CLEAN agree=68 diverge=0`**; `make -C rust parse_harness_equivalence_gate` → **4 passed** — `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` now includes `return_annotation`; the **ratchet** confirmed the promotion (leaving only `rtl_const_expr` DEFERRED); `every_registered_grammar_is_classified_exactly_once`; `comment_arm_suppression_matrix_is_pinned` unaffected. Interpreter unit tests **7/7**; `unified_return_ast` serialization round-trip tests **27/27**.
- **No-regression (measured):** the shared serialization change affects ONLY grammars whose LR-eliminated rules carry **Object** templates — a repo-wide audit found exactly TWO (`return_annotation`, `semantic_annotation`); both regenerated, both byte-identical in the gate (`semantic_annotation` stays CERTIFIED). NO `ast_shape_contract` manifest pins a `wrapper_specs` blob (grep-verified); the FINAL folded AST is a `serde_json::Value` built by the fold (already sorted) and is unaffected. **Emit-neutrality proof on the big grammar:** `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` REGENERATED `systemverilog_parser.rs` with the modified `ast_pipeline` → IDENTICAL cert (canonical **1343/10/1321/12**, union residual `["context_member_method_call"]`, `sample_parse_failures=0`, deterministic seeds 0/7/42, `unmet_criteria_count=0`) — SV has no Object-template `wrapper_specs`. New code clippy-clean; `mdbook_docs_gate` GREEN.
- **Novel/surfaced (director, `feedback_surface_insights_prominently` + `feedback_be_alert_root_cause_fishy_immediately`):** the fix incidentally closed a **latent codegen non-determinism** — before this leaf, the generated parsers' `wrapper_specs` blobs were frozen from a non-deterministic std `HashMap`, so two `--generate-parser` runs could freeze DIFFERENT (behaviorally-equivalent) orders; now byte-identical across regens (tool-verified: regen twice → `diff` empty). Broader latent risk worth an audit tree: **are there OTHER `serde`-serialized std `HashMap`s frozen into generated artifacts** (a general codegen-determinism sweep)? Also: the scouting-log hypothesis being right on SYMPTOM (key-order) but wrong on CAUSE (mirrorable order vs non-deterministic artifact) reaffirms `feedback_no_codebase_change_without_tool_backed_facts` — the byte-level scout, not the plausible theory, is what settled it.
- **Lockstep (director D5 directive, SAME-COMMIT):** top-level mdBook `docs/book/src/parse-harness.md` (CERTIFIED/DEFERRED table → 10/1; new *Canonical serialization of the LR-chain blob* subsection; the "9→10" counts); `TOOLBOX.md` §1.6; tree `PARSE-HARNESS.md` (`.5.3` done + §18 checklist, frontier → `.5.5`, §15 map); DEVELOPMENT_NOTES + MEMORY + LIVE status.

## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0009 (PARSE-HARNESS.5.2): ebnf fidelity — per-introducer comment-arm suppression promotes `ebnf` DEFERRED→CERTIFIED (9th grammar)

Session #43. **CODE leaf — interpreter-tooling + an additive shared codegen query, parser-AGNOSTIC: edits `rust/src/parse_harness_interpreter.rs` (gate the two layout skippers' comment arms), `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_based_generator.rs` (a NEW `pub(crate)` read-only query `comment_arm_suppression_for_grammar` + `CommentArmSuppression`), `rust/src/ast_pipeline/ast_generator_direct.rs` (`snake_to_pascal` → `pub(crate)`), `rust/src/parse_harness_equivalence.rs` (promote `ebnf`; generalize the deep-stress probe + a matrix-pinning gate test); NO engine / grammar / codegen-EMIT / generated-parser change; no release/schema bump.** Closes the interpreter's ebnf divergence, taking the differential-equivalence gate from **8 → 9 CERTIFIED** grammars.

- **Reproduced (BEFORE):** `PGEN_PHEQ_ONLY=ebnf …::measurement` (ladder [6,12,18], seeds 0/7/42) → `ebnf DIVERGE samples=83 agree=77 diverge=6`. All 6 one class — the interpreter ACCEPTS a comment/layout-only input the generated ebnf parser REJECTS: `"/**/"` (interp furthest=3), `"/*"` (furthest=2), `"       /**//***/"` (furthest=10) + 3 more of the same shape.
- **Root cause (WHY+WHERE — TOOLS-FIRST, by reading the EMITTED oracle + the codegen it comes from; full detail `docs/tasks/PARSE-HARNESS.md` §17):** the generated ebnf parser's `consume_layout_for_terminal` (`generated/ebnf.rs:70486-70523`) has arms for `#` and `//` but **NO `/* */` block-comment arm**. This is codegen's per-introducer static suppression (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.11.5): `terminal_block_comment_arm = if claims_block_comment { EMPTY } else { EMIT }` (`ast_based_generator.rs:4713-4733`), where `claims_block_comment = grammar_claims_introducer_as_non_comment(tree, "/*")` (`:4522`) is **true** for ebnf because `block_comment := "/*" block_comment_content "*/"` (`grammars/ebnf.ebnf:560`) makes `"/*"` a real, non-comment grammar token — so codegen does NOT skip `/* */` as layout and requires structural matching. The interpreter's two layout skippers (`parse_harness_interpreter.rs:1044-1101` / `:1103-1167`) **unconditionally** skipped all three comment introducers, so on `/**/` it skipped the block comment as layout, reached EOF, and ACCEPTed. The per-grammar arm matrix was read from ALL 10 generated parsers (json/svpp/rtl_const_expr/return_annotation = all 3 arms; regex/vhdl/systemverilog/rtl_frontend = no `#`; semantic_annotation = `#` only; ebnf = no `/*`) — the interpreter's unconditional arms are a LATENT over-skip for every suppressed cell; ebnf's `/*` is simply the first the corpus witnessed.
- **Fix (fix-hierarchy tier = new interpreter tooling + an ADDITIVE shared codegen query — single source of truth, no drift; the codegen EMIT path is NOT touched):** the interpreter computes the per-introducer suppression via codegen's OWN predicate `grammar_claims_introducer_as_non_comment` (exposed as `comment_arm_suppression_for_grammar`, which reconstructs codegen's minimal generator config — `AstBasedGenerator::new(snake_to_pascal(name))` + `.annotations`), and gates each of the three arms in both layout skippers on it. Because the interpreter now computes the IDENTICAL booleans codegen emits with, it can never drift; a new gate test pins the per-grammar `(#, //, /*)` matrix against the shipped parsers. General ⇒ also removed the latent over-skip for regex/vhdl/sv/rtl_frontend (`#`) and semantic_annotation (`//`+`/*`).
- **Addressed (verified — re-runnable oracles):** `PGEN_PHEQ_ONLY=ebnf …::measurement` `DIVERGE 6` → **`CLEAN agree=83 diverge=0`**; `make -C rust parse_harness_equivalence_gate` → **4 passed** — `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` now includes `ebnf`; the **ratchet** (`deferred_grammars_are_still_divergent_or_promote_them`) confirmed the promotion; the new `comment_arm_suppression_matrix_is_pinned` locks the matrix; completeness holds. Interpreter unit tests **7/7**. Deep-stress (`probe_layout_deep_stress`, ebnf widened to 5 seeds × the gate depths [6,12,18] — its no-memo deep recursion is impractical past depth ~18, the `.6` memoization is that fix) → **CLEAN 242/242**.
- **No-regression (measured):** interpreter-tooling + an additive `pub(crate)` query (codegen EMIT path unchanged) — `git status` shows only the 4 source files (+ docs); **no `generated/*_parser.rs` regenerated** → the 8 previously-certified grammars + SV byte-identical by construction, re-proven by `certified_grammars_are_byte_identical` (the shared predicate makes the interpreter match codegen for ALL grammars → the arm gating can only REDUCE divergence, never introduce it). SV cert re-verified via `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` → canonical **1343/10/1321/12** (seeds 0/7/42, unchanged). New code clippy-clean.
- **Novel/surfaced (director, `feedback_surface_insights_prominently`):** the fidelity fix here is the CLEAN counterpoint to `.5.1`'s name-gate tension — `comment_arm_suppression` is a genuine GRAMMAR-PROPERTY query (does any rule claim this introducer as a non-comment token?), not a grammar-name switch. By having the interpreter call codegen's OWN predicate rather than re-implement the deep regex-HIR analysis, the two implementations share one kernel and cannot desync — the strongest form of the "mirror the generator" discipline (contrast `.5.1`'s `LayoutPolicy`, which mirrors three trivial name-normalized booleans).
- **Lockstep (director D5 directive, SAME-COMMIT):** top-level mdBook `docs/book/src/parse-harness.md` (CERTIFIED/DEFERRED table → 9/2; new *Comment layout is grammar-specific* subsection; the "8→9" counts); `TOOLBOX.md` §1.6; tree `PARSE-HARNESS.md` (`.5.2` done + §17 checklist, frontier → `.5.3`/`.5.5`, §15 map); DEVELOPMENT_NOTES + MEMORY + LIVE status.
- **Release/schema:** UNCHANGED (SV `1.0.167` / schema `16`) — interpreter tooling only.

## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0005 (PARSE-HARNESS.5): the differential-equivalence GATE — the certifying oracle that makes the interpreter authoritative-by-verification

Session #41. **CODE leaf — purely additive tooling, parser-AGNOSTIC: a new module `rust/src/parse_harness_equivalence.rs` + one `#[cfg(all(feature="ebnf_dual_run", feature="generated_parsers"))] pub mod parse_harness_equivalence;` line in `rust/src/lib.rs` + one `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` Makefile target; NO existing grammar/parser/codegen/runtime/registry path touched; no release/schema bump.** Delivers the leg that earns the interpreter's (`.4`) trust: the deterministic interpreter-vs-generated-parser differential over the registered-grammar corpus.

It genuinely DIVERGES on 4 (`regex` — greediness-fold AST + a deeper `\Q…\E`-quantifier/`!"\\E"`-lookahead verdict divergence; `ebnf` — a verdict divergence; `return_annotation` — a positional-ref/`Json` fold AST divergence; `systemverilog_preprocessor` — a span/shape AST divergence), has NO corpus for `rtl_const_expr` (deep precedence chain exceeds bounded generation depth; unbounded deep gen hangs — the known super-linear pathology), and CANNOT apply to `builtin_return_annotation`/`builtin_semantic_annotation` (their registry oracle is an alias of the `return_annotation` parser / a hand-rolled `parse_bootstrap`, `parser_registry.rs:218,232` — not codegen of their own `.ebnf`). Requires BOTH `ebnf_dual_run` (the `.ebnf` loader + stimuli corpus) AND `generated_parsers` (the `parser_registry` oracle) — the module is correctly EXCLUDED otherwise (a cfg bug the SV-cert `ebnf_dual_run`-only build first caught, then fixed).

The new module is clippy-clean; correctly excluded under an `ebnf_dual_run`-only build (`cargo check --features ebnf_dual_run` clean). `mdbook_docs_gate` GREEN.

## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0004 (PARSE-HARNESS.4): the grammar-AST interpreter core — parse an ARBITRARY grammar IN-PROCESS with NO codegen / NO compile (parse-harness approach 1, authoritative BY VERIFICATION)

Session #40, fresh session (per the tree's recommendation before this heavier Phase-B work). **CODE leaf — purely additive tooling, parser-AGNOSTIC: a new module `rust/src/parse_harness_interpreter.rs` + one `pub mod parse_harness_interpreter;` line in `rust/src/lib.rs`; NO existing grammar/parser/codegen/runtime/registry path touched; no release/schema bump.** Delivers PARSE-HARNESS approach 1 (the director's flagship — the only harness NOT authoritative-by-construction), opening **Phase B**; its trust is *earned* by a differential-equivalence oracle (the `.3` compile-and-run harness + the registry), not assumed.

- **Reproduced (BEFORE):** the two Phase-A harnesses (scratch slot `.2`, compile-and-run `.3`) close the arbitrary-grammar gap authoritatively-by-construction but each pays a per-probe **codegen + `rustc` compile** (seconds→minutes). There was no **fast, in-process, no-compile** way to parse an input against an arbitrary grammar — the daily grammar-authoring / linter-soundness probe shape, and the fast side of the `.5` differential gate.
- **Root cause / the make-or-break design fact (WHY+WHERE — tool-mapped this session, recorded in `docs/tasks/PARSE-HARNESS.md` §13):** an interpreter is a genuine *second* parsing implementation, so its "thin dynamic-dispatch layer" boundary had to be established before writing a line. Two code-mapping passes over the tree established it precisely: a generated parser's **combinator control-flow is fully inlined per-rule as codegen `quote!` templates** — there is NO shared runtime `impl` for it — while the **semantic + type layer is callable runtime** (`semantic_runtime.rs` / `mod.rs`, all `pub`). So the interpreter splits into: **Section A (reuse VERBATIM)** — `ParseNode`/`ParseContent` (byte-identical serde), `parse_quantifier_bounds`, `SemanticRuntimeState` checkpoint/rollback, the `ASTNode` IR + in-process loader; **Section B (re-express — parser-agnostic, mirrored byte-for-byte from a generated parser's emitted code)** — `match_string`/`match_regex`/the layout consumers/`try_parse`; **Section C (re-express the dispatch)** — the ordered-choice tournament + `branch_policy`, sequence, the quantifier loop, lookahead, and the return-annotation fold. Every shape rule was read from the authoritative generated `json`/`rtl_const_expr` parsers (atom→`Terminal`/`Alternative`, the `should_take` longest-match ladder, the synthetic `-> $1` passthrough for single-element bodies, the quantifier iteration node `rule_name:"quantified"`/`span:0..0`, `captured_vars==["result"]` at every fold call site).
- **Fix (fix-hierarchy tier = new tooling / plumbing — no engine, annotation, grammar, codegen, or existing-runtime change):** `rust/src/parse_harness_interpreter.rs` exposes `interpret_parse(grammar_ebnf, input, &InterpretOptions) -> Result<ParseOutcome, InterpretError>` (loads the `.ebnf` → normalized gen-AST via `ebnf_frontend` + `RustASTPipeline::transform_from_raw_ast`, then dispatches) and the feature-independent core `interpret_parse_gen_ast(tree, order, anns, entry, input)` (the `.5`-gate entry). It returns the SAME `crate::parse_harness::ParseOutcome` as `compile_and_parse`, so the two are directly diffable. A **process-global interner** leaks the finite set of grammar-derived strings (rule names, quantifier labels, annotation literals) to `&'static str` so the exact shipped `ParseNode` type is reused → byte-identical serialized AST. `SemanticRuntimeState` is threaded through `try_parse` (speculation snapshots it faithfully) so `.6` extends without restructuring. Boundary logging routes through the shared `pgen_trace*` macros.
- **Addressed (verified — the capability now exists, byte-identical to the authoritative parser):** re-runnable oracles = two differential tests. (1) `interpreter_is_byte_identical_to_the_json_registry_parser` (`#[cfg(all(feature="generated_parsers", feature="ebnf_dual_run", has_generated_json_parser))]`) — the interpreter's verdict + typed `ast_json` are **byte-identical to `parser_registry::parse_sample_ast_json("json", …)`** across 7 accepts + 4 rejects (exercising multi-branch `Or`/longest_match, single-branch rules, `Sequence`, regex tokens, `rule_reference` recursion, the object/array/spread return-annotation fold, and layout). (2) `interpreter_agrees_with_compile_and_run_on_synthetic_combinators` (`#[cfg(feature="ebnf_dual_run")]`) — verdict + `furthest_position` + typed AST **byte-identical to `compile_and_parse`** on 5 synthetic per-combinator grammars: the A2.3 fixed-terminal-prefix shape (`start := "a" | "a" "b"` — longest_match accepts `"ab"` where ordered would reject), `*`/`+` repetition, optional `?`, and `&`/`!` lookahead. Plus 5 unit tests (interner dedup, integer-typing, synthetic-passthrough rule, Alternative-peel, empty-regex probe). `cargo test --lib --features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run" parse_harness_interpreter` → **7 passed; 0 failed**.
- **No-regression (measured):** purely additive tooling never invoked by any parse/codegen/cert path — `git status` shows only `rust/src/parse_harness_interpreter.rs` (new), `rust/src/lib.rs`, and docs; **no `generated/*_parser.rs` regenerated** (mtimes unchanged), so the 6 fully-certified grammars + SV are **byte-identical by construction**. SV cert re-verified via `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` at seeds 0/7/42 → canonical **1343/10/1321/12**, union **1343/10/1332/1**, `sample_parse_failures=0`. The new module is **clippy-clean** (0 findings; the 179 generated-stage `eq_op` errors are pre-existing, unchanged). `mdbook_docs_gate` GREEN. Full lib builds with `--features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run"`.
- **Honest bounds (stated, not hidden — `PARSE-HARNESS.md` §3.4/§13.4):** the `.4` **core** is byte-identical on the **structural + return-annotation** surface + verdict + `furthest_position` (proven on the smoke set). Deferred to `.5`/`.6` (threaded, not in the `.4` smoke set): the semantic-directive orchestration that *gates parse outcomes* on the store (`@predicate`/`@emit_fact`), the non-default `branch_policy`/`@priority` paths, packrat memoization (a transparent AST-invariant cache — added where the full corpus needs it), and full-corpus byte-identity. Bounded `{N,M}` quantifiers are honored by `parse_quantified` but are not reachable from `.ebnf` input syntax yet (documented in-test). No over-claim of a formal all-inputs proof.
- **Lockstep (director D5 directive, SAME-COMMIT, non-negotiable):** top-level mdBook `docs/book/src/parse-harness.md` gains the **grammar-AST interpreter** section (to the depth of the scratch-slot / compile-and-run / linter / stimuli-gen / parser-gen chapters: what it is, the API + core entry, the by-verification trust argument, the shared-core boundary, the interning-to-`'static` subtlety, honest bounds) + the approaches table row promoted `forthcoming → core landed`; `TOOLBOX.md` §1.5 interpreter entry + quick-chooser row; tree `PARSE-HARNESS.md` (`.4` in-progress→checklist + §13 plan; frontier); DEVELOPMENT_NOTES + MEMORY + LIVE status.

## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-PARSE-HARNESS-0003 (PARSE-HARNESS.3): the compile-and-run harness — parse an ARBITRARY grammar via a throwaway EXTERNAL compile, NO registry edit / NO `pgen` rebuild (parse-harness approach 2, authoritative BY CONSTRUCTION)

Session #39, PNT continuation. **CODE leaf — purely additive tooling, parser-AGNOSTIC: a new module `rust/src/parse_harness.rs` + one `pub mod parse_harness;` line in `rust/src/lib.rs`; NO existing grammar/parser/codegen/runtime/registry path touched; no release/schema bump.** Delivers PARSE-HARNESS approach 2 (the second authoritative-by-construction harness), completing **Phase A** of the tree; it is the self-contained CI oracle for the `.5` differential-equivalence gate.

- **Reproduced (BEFORE):** the scratch slot (`.2`) closes the arbitrary-grammar gap for the CLI toolbox but needs a permanent registry slot + a `pgen`/probe rebuild per body change. There was no **self-contained, in-process** way to compile+run the real parser for an arbitrary `.ebnf` (no registry edit, no `pgen` rebuild) — the shape a Rust gate/oracle can call directly (needed by `.5`).
- **Root cause / make-or-break feasibility (WHY+WHERE, tool-verified this session):** a generated parser's source hard-codes `use crate::ast_pipeline::{…}` (`generated/*_parser.rs:3`). Inside `pgen` that resolves against the whole crate (incl. `pub(crate)` items); an **external** throwaway crate sees only `pub` items, so it was not obvious a generated parser could compile outside `pgen` at all. Decisive evidence: (1) static audit — `grep -oE "crate::ast_pipeline::[A-Za-z_]+"` over **all** `generated/*_parser.rs` → **22 distinct symbols, every one `pub`**; the only externs are `regex`/`rustc_hash`/`serde_json`; `ParseNode` derives `serde::Serialize` (`ast_pipeline/mod.rs:754`) so the throwaway serializes the **byte-identical** typed AST the registry's `parse_node_to_json` = `serde_json::to_value(node)` (`parser_registry.rs:1044`) does. (2) empirical spike — an external crate that path-deps `pgen`, adds the single shim `use pgen::ast_pipeline;` (making `crate::ast_pipeline::…` resolve to `pgen`'s), and `include!`s the generated file **compiled and ran**, reproducing registry verdicts on TWO grammars with distinct machinery (`scratch` "hello, world!"→ACCEPT / "hello, mars!"→REJECT `furthest=7`; `json` `{"a":1,…}`→ACCEPT / `{"a": }`→REJECT `furthest=6`). Exactly one `pub struct <Name>Parser<'input>` per generated file (verified across 7 grammars) → the struct name is discoverable by grep, no re-derivation. Also verified: one-step `ast_pipeline foo.ebnf --generate-parser -o …` is byte-identical to the shipped two-step `RUST_GENERATOR` recipe except the embedded diagnostic output-path label (inert; never in the AST), and `--debug`/`--trace` are pure logging (droppable).
- **Fix (fix-hierarchy tier = new tooling / plumbing — no engine, annotation, grammar, codegen, or registry change):** `rust/src/parse_harness.rs` exposes `compile_and_parse(grammar_ebnf, input, &CompileAndParseOptions) -> Result<ParseOutcome, HarnessError>`. It (1) shells the pre-built `ast_pipeline` binary once (`.ebnf → parser.rs`, the shipped recipe minus logging flags), (2) discovers the parser struct name by grep, (3) synthesizes a throwaway external crate (path-dep `pgen` + the `use pgen::ast_pipeline;` shim; isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` → no lock contention with an outer `cargo test`), (4) `cargo build`s it, (5) runs it on the input (via a file, so arbitrary bytes survive; `parse_full()` / `parse_full_from(entry)` → entry-rule-agnostic) and marshals its sentinel-fenced JSON back into `ParseOutcome {accepted, furthest_position, error, ast_json}`. A parse *rejection* is a successful `Ok(ParseOutcome{accepted:false})`; `HarnessError` is reserved for genuine plumbing failures, each carrying the failing step + captured tool output. Boundary logging routes through the shared `pgen_trace*` macros (README tracing doctrine).
- **Addressed (verified — the capability now exists):** re-runnable oracle = the `#[cfg(all(feature="generated_parsers", has_generated_json_parser))]` integration test `parse_harness::tests::compile_and_run_harness_reproduces_json_registry_verdict_and_ast` — **1 passed** — which drives `grammars/json.ebnf` through the harness and asserts, for `{"a": 1, "b": [true, null, "x"]}`: `accepted==true` AND `ast_json == parser_registry::parse_sample_ast_json("json", …)` (**byte-identical** typed AST to the shipped registry), and for `{"a": }`: `accepted==false` matching `parse_sample("json", …)==Some(false)`. Plus 5 unit tests (struct-name discovery incl. ambiguity refusal, sentinel/JSON marshalling, reject shape). `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers parse_harness` → **6 passed; 0 failed**.
- **No-regression (measured):** purely additive tooling never invoked by any parse/codegen/cert path — `git status` shows only `rust/src/parse_harness.rs` (new), `rust/src/lib.rs`, and the two docs files; **no `generated/*_parser.rs` regenerated** (mtimes unchanged), so the 6 fully-certified grammars + SV are **byte-identical by construction**. SV cert re-verified via `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` at seeds 0/7/42 → canonical **1343/10/1321/12**, union **1343/10/1332/1**, `sample_parse_failures=0`. `parse_harness` is **clippy-clean** (`cargo clippy --lib --tests --features generated_parsers` — 0 findings in the module; the 179 generated-stage `eq_op` errors are pre-existing, unchanged). `mdbook_docs_gate` GREEN. Full lib builds with `--features generated_parsers`.
- **Lockstep (director D5 directive, SAME-COMMIT, non-negotiable):** top-level mdBook `docs/book/src/parse-harness.md` gains the **compile-and-run harness** section to the depth of the scratch-slot / linter / stimuli-gen / parser-gen chapters (API, 5-step plumbing, the load-bearing external-compile fact, by-construction trust, cost/reuse) + the approaches table row promoted `forthcoming → landed`; `TOOLBOX.md` §1.4 compile-and-run entry; tree `PARSE-HARNESS.md` (`.3` done + checklist; Phase A complete; frontier → `.4`); DEVELOPMENT_NOTES + MEMORY.
- **Release/schema:** UNCHANGED (SV `1.0.167` / schema `16`) — additive tooling only, no consumer-visible parser behavior change.

## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0150 (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.A2.2): RETIRE the unsound `EarlierAlwaysMatches` shadowing verdict + its bogus certificate; DEMOTE the always-succeeds observation to a non-verdict `[note]`

The certifying linter was emitting an unsound deadness VERDICT on a proven-LIVE branch (violates [[feedback_certifying_linter_trustworthiness]] "the linter NEVER declares a live fragment dead").
- **Root cause (WHY+WHERE):** `grammar_wellformedness.rs` `collect_shadowing` concluded "earlier alt always-succeeds ⇒ later alt `ShadowingReason::EarlierAlwaysMatches` (unreachable)"; the message stated the false premise "PEG commits to the earlier alternative". PGEN does NOT commit-to-first (backtracking / `longest_match` policy) — `compute_always_succeeds` is correct, the "⇒ unreachable" conclusion is unsound (tool-proven at `A2.1-SOUNDNESS`).
- **Fix (ENGINE tier — a linter/analysis soundness fix, not expressible in the grammar or an annotation; DISPOSITION = demote, no sound sub-case exists):** removed `ShadowingReason::EarlierAlwaysMatches` (enum + detection + `message`/`certificate` arms) so `detect_ordered_choice_shadowing` yields ONLY the two genuinely-sound reasons (exact-duplicate + fixed-terminal-prefix); removed the unsound `UnreachabilityReason::EarlierArmAlwaysSucceeds` certificate variant + its verifier arms (a certificate is a PROOF of deadness, which always-succeeds cannot supply); removed the now-vacuous `ShadowingReason::is_hard_gate`; added the non-verdict `WellformednessIssue::AlwaysSucceedsAlternative` + detector `detect_always_succeeds_alternatives` (mirrors `detect_nullable_repetition`), whose `message()` makes NO unreachability claim. `main.rs --lint-grammar` header field `always_matches_shadowing` → `always_succeeds_alternatives={N} (note)`; notes print as `[note]`; the `shadow_hard`/`shadow_warn` partition removed (every surviving `ShadowingReason` gates).
- **Addressed (verified):** after — `--lint-grammar` on SV reports `always_succeeds_alternatives=6 (note)` (the former 8 warnings; the count reframes "one per shadowed victim" → "one per always-succeeding source"), `ordered_choice_shadowing=0` unchanged, rc=0; 0 `is unreachable`/`PEG commits` strings in the note channel; the proven-live `net_port_type_sv_2017 #2` interconnect branch is no longer flagged at all.
- **No-regression (measured):** `cargo test -p pgen --lib grammar_wellformedness` 40/40 GREEN (shadowing/certificate/note suites updated); `--lint-grammar` rc=0 on all 7 shipped grammars (hard gate exact-dup + fixed-prefix both 0; the 6 fully-certified grammars at `always_succeeds_alternatives=0`); canonical cert-coverage byte-identical `1343/10/1321/12` at seeds 0/7/42 via `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate` (shadowing certs are branch-level, NOT in the rule-level proof pool — `grammar_wellformedness.rs`, so the headline is provably unmoved). NO grammar/parser/generated change ⇒ 6 fully-certified grammars byte-identical.
- **Lockstep:** book `docs/book/src/grammar-wellformedness.md` (the "As implemented (A2.2)" note + reconciled the "Where PGEN stands" + intro + worked-example framing to the retire+demote disposition); decision `project_earlier_always_matches_unsound_backtracking` (disposition IMPLEMENTED + a logged `A2.3` `FixedTerminalPrefix` soundness follow-up); tree `A2.2` leaf + frontier + TASK_TREE row; MEMORY.

## 2026-07-05 - PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0149 (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.A2.1-SOUNDNESS): 🚨 the A2 `EarlierAlwaysMatches` linter check is UNSOUND for PGEN's backtracking engine — it declares a proven-LIVE fragment dead; the A2.1 hard-gate promotion is RETIRED

Session #37, PNT continuation. **INVESTIGATION leaf — ZERO code (pure docs); no grammar/parser/engine change, no regen, no release/schema bump.** Surfaced while verifying the deferred A2.1 residual 8 tools-first (the first time those branches were checked against the REAL parser rather than reasoned from grammar shape).

- **Finding:** the grammar linter's `always_matches_shadowing` check (`ShadowingReason::EarlierAlwaysMatches`, landed by `A2`) is UNSOUND for PGEN's BACKTRACKING engine. Its verdict premise — "alternative #0 always matches … (PEG commits to the earlier alternative)" — is FALSE for PGEN, which backtracks (enters alternatives in turn, keeps the one that leads to overall success). It therefore **declares a live fragment dead**, violating the [[feedback_certifying_linter_trustworthiness]] contract ("the linter NEVER declares a live fragment dead").
- **Decisive evidence (existing shipped parser, NO regen — three independent tool angles):** for `module m(interconnect p);` (`--profile sv_2017`, ACCEPTS) the linter flags `net_port_type_sv_2017` alt #2 unreachable, but (1) `--parse-dump-ast-pretty` shows `{kind:"interconnect"}` in the FINAL AST via the net_port_type route; (2) producer-grep — that alt #2 (`net_port_type_interconnect_sv_only`, `systemverilog.ebnf:3490`) is the only interconnect producer reachable in a PORT context (the other, `:3444`, is a `;`-terminated net *declaration*); (3) `--trace-rules net_port_type_sv_2017` — the parser ENTERS branch 1/3, 2/3, AND 3/3 (alt #0 matches zero-length; branch 3 wins). A branch entered AND present in the final tree is REACHED → "unreachable" is a FALSE POSITIVE.
- **Root cause:** `compute_always_succeeds` is correct (alt #0 `( net_type )? data_type_or_implicit` always-succeeds because `implicit_data_type` is nullable), but the CONCLUSION "⇒ later alternatives unreachable" holds only under PEG-commit. The sound property under backtracking is "can this alt ever WIN" — a language-difference question, undecidable in general (the class the certifying-linter decision EXCLUDES alongside general FIRST-domination + parse-order predicate reachability).
- **Re-adjudication:** A2.1's "promote `EarlierAlwaysMatches` to a hard gate" goal is RETIRED; the 8 residual `always_matches` warnings include FALSE POSITIVES (the port-header/net-type family fires via backtracking), NOT dead branches; item-4b store-gating is NOT an A2 deadness fix (the branches are reachable). The earlier A2.1 dropped-delimiter fixes (boolean-abbrev, covergroup, rs-prod, module-path) were LRM-correct on their own merits and STAND — only the deadness LABEL + gate goal are retracted. FRONTIER → `A2.2` (decide the check's disposition — retire / demote to a non-verdict hint / restrict to a provably-sound sub-case — + drop the `is_hard_gate` path in `grammar_wellformedness.rs`).
- **Recorded (lockstep):** tree `A2.1-SOUNDNESS` + `A2.2` frontier + TASK_TREE row; decision `project_earlier_always_matches_unsound_backtracking.md` + index; book `grammar-wellformedness.md` (corrected the "three sound forms" claim + a "⚠️ Correction (2026-07-05)" callout under the worked example + the "sound decidable subset" caveat; mdbook gate GREEN); MEMORY.
- **Release/schema:** UNCHANGED (SV `1.0.167` / schema `16`). NO code change of any kind.

The grammar over-specified by keeping BOTH `;`s.

## 2026-07-04 - PGEN-SV-LRM-SHAPE-FIDELITY-0001 (SV-LRM-SHAPE-FIDELITY.1): `SV-0024` CLOSED — un-braced multi-identifier port lists no longer over-accept; braced concatenation ports now accepted; SV release 1.0.164 → 1.0.165, schema 15 unchanged

IEEE `port_expression ::= port_reference | { port_reference {, port_reference} }` requires LITERAL concatenation braces for the multi-reference form, so `a b` is invalid.
- **Root cause (WHY+WHERE, AST-dump-pinned).** Two accepting paths, one per profile: (1) **verilog_2005 (non-ANSI):** `--parse-dump-ast-pretty --profile verilog_2005` shows `port_expression {kind:"list", body:[{name:a…},{name:b…}]}` — WHERE: `port_expression`'s second alternative (`grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:4092`) `( port_reference ( comma port_reference )* )*`, an un-braced `*`-repeated group with no `lbrace`/`rbrace`/separator (the LRM's literal concatenation braces were extracted as BNF meta-repetition). (2) **sv_2017/sv_2023 (ANSI):** `--parse-dump-ast-pretty --profile sv_2017` shows `{kind:"net_or_interface", header:{kind:"named", name:a}, name:b}` — `a` parsed as an `interface_port_header` (`:2691`), `b` as the port name; this is a DIFFERENT path exposed after the `SV-0037` fix (`.3.1`) store-gated `net_port_type`.
- **Spec re-adjudication (from the LRM, independent of the stale ledger repro).** The ledger row predated `SV-0037`; post-`.3.1` sv_2017's `a b` is the legitimate ANSI interface-port path. Per IEEE 1800 A.1.3 `interface_port_header port_identifier` IS a valid ANSI interface port (the "`a` is not a declared interface" check is elaboration, not parse). So the spec-faithful outcome is: `a b` REJECTS under `verilog_2005` (no interfaces there — only `port_expression`, which needs braces), ACCEPTS under `sv_2017`/`sv_2023` (interface port). Measured pre-fix: `module m ({a, b});` REJECTS under BOTH profiles (the braced concat port was unsupported — the un-braced alt never matched `{`), so the fix simultaneously ADDS the missing correct form and REMOVES the invalid one.
- **Fix (declarative, grammar-only):** restored the LRM shape — `port_expression`'s second alternative → `lbrace port_reference ( comma port_reference )* rbrace -> {kind:"list", body:[$2, $3::2*]}` (the established `assignment_pattern` concatenation-list idiom). ZERO new rules (census `1465`). No hand-written source touched. `port_expression` is referenced only at `port` (`:4066`/`:4068`) — contained blast radius; NO `ast_shape_contract` sample references it.
- **Addressed (verified, release binary):** `module m (a b);` flips ACCEPT→**REJECT** under `verilog_2005`; ACCEPT unchanged under `sv_2017`/`sv_2023` (interface port); `module m ({a, b});` / `({a, b, c})` flip REJECT→**ACCEPT** under EVERY profile (braced concat, new `{kind:"list", body:[refs]}` shape); single / comma-separated / named `.p(a)` / ANSI-declaration ports unchanged.

- **The WHY, tool-named (one scoped debug-trace cert run, stdout+stderr piped through a grep — no multi-GB artifact):** the name-prelude arms CORRECTLY (`gated_rule='known_unscoped_property_identifier' kind='property_name' producer='declared_property_identifier' clean_path=true site=('source_text','root')`), but the INJECTED declaration construct must derive the producer's host `property_declaration` INCLUDING its deep mandatory sibling `property_spec` (~25-level expression chain), and the per-target witness budget never accounts for the prelude sub-path — tier-1 is `reach_prefix + min_subtree[target]`, tier-2 adds `max_offpath_mandatory_sibling_depth` over the MAIN hop chain only. The forced property branch dies with `Stimuli generation depth exceeded max_depth=64 while expanding rule 'number'`; `generate_or`'s forced-first-with-fallback then silently selects `sequence_declaration`, and the injection loop accepts any `Ok` render without verifying the armed `(kind, family)` fact was emitted → the prelude registers `sequence_name`, useless to the `has_fact(property_name)` gate.
- **Why HEAD still witnesses / why the `.6.3` lifts break it:** at HEAD the main chain hosts the use-site inside `property_declaration`, whose own `declared_property_identifier` self-emits `property_name` (the replay echoes it — `render='\foo_0'`); the `.6.3` lifts re-roll the BFS to the top-level `bind` route with NO property host on path, so the gate depends entirely on the wrong-kind prelude → the recorded 48/48 failures (= 4 attempts × 2 tiers × 2 entry-configs × 3 seeds).
- **Control that isolates the blind spot:** the direct `declared_property_identifier` probe has NO prelude armed, fails tier-1 4× with the SAME depth error, and IS rescued by tier-2 (its deep sibling is on the MAIN chain, visible to the tier-2 scan) — witnessed `property\foo ;2737.2682endproperty`. The defect is specific to the armed-prelude sub-path.
- **Fix commissioned (`.6.3.2`, new frontier — engine, general/parser-agnostic):** armed-prelude fact-kind integrity check (`store_name_for_gate`) after each injected render + ONE depth-fresh retry from the injection depth (the proven H.4.2 constructive-reach pattern) before failing the attempt. Blast radius = armed name-preludes only (99 armings / 10 gated rules in the canonical run); count-preludes and already-correct injections stay byte-identical. `.6.3` replays after it.

The property-layer dual of the 1.0.148 sequence cascade — the second and final half of the `H.12.5.8` SVA infix left-recursion class.

- **REPRODUCE / ISSUE:** the IEEE 1800 §16 SVA **property** infix operators `until`/`s_until`/`until_with`/`s_until_with` (and property-level `iff`, and `or`/`and` over property operands like `(always a) or (always b)`) were REJECTED at the operator on every release ≤ 1.0.148; the 4 `until`-family keywords (property-only) were the SV cert residual. Same defect class as the sequence-layer `SV-0010`.
- **FIX:** restructured both profiles into the IEEE 1800-2017 §16 (Table 16-3) binary-infix precedence cascade — `property_expr_sv_<profile> := prop_until_sv_<profile> -> $1` over 5 new `prop_*` rules/profile (`prop_until > prop_iff > prop_or > prop_and > prop_primary`, all right-associative inline `head op self` so no tail rules); `prop_primary` keeps every non-LR branch byte-identical (bodies still reference the `property_expr` dispatch). REUSES the `prefer_sole_reference_passthrough_sites` engine fix landed with SV-0010 (no engine change). Schema-preserving hybrid: only the binary infix bug is cascaded; the loose unary/impl/temporal ops keep their correct bind-whole-rhs dispatch precedence.
- **ADDRESSED (verified):** SV cert `UNKNOWN 26 → 22` (4 until-family witnessed; `total 1299→1304`, `witness 1272→1281`; deterministic seeds 0/7/42; `spf=0`; zero newly-unknown — set-diff = exactly the 4 until-family). Parse matrix REJECT→PASS with correct precedence (`a until b iff c` ⇒ `until(a,iff(b,c))`; `a and b or c` ⇒ `or(and(a,b),c)`); previously-parsing forms (`not not a`/`always a`/`a #-# b`/`accept_on(a) b`) byte-identical carriers.
- **NO REGRESSION:** the 6 fully-certified grammars byte-identical (grammar-only, SV-isolated); SV external corpus 14/14 (`parse_fail_total=0`); `ast_shape_contract` 18/18; `--lint-grammar` clean (`1425` rules, +10; `non_terminating=0`, `unreachable_rules=0`, `ordered_choice_shadowing=0`, `profile_orphans=0`); clippy source-clean (generated `eq_op` debt pre-existing, non-strict).

(5) DECISIVE `--parse` A/B (parser unchanged ⇒ generator-agnostic): `module m;int \foo ;initial case(\foo .\bar .\baz ())default:;endcase endmodule` → dumped AST `"kind":"context_member_method"` count **= 1** (WITNESSES); but `program p(input logic a);\foo ;case(+\foo .\foo .\foo )default:;endcase endprogram` (head ALSO `\foo`) → count **= 0** — a bare UNTYPED `\foo ;` does NOT parse as a `variable_decl_assignment` emitting `variable_binding \foo`, so the gate has no fact to match even with the head echoing. The generator's minimal `data_declaration` renders the untyped branch; forcing the TYPED branch (`int \foo ;`) is a NEW prelude-derivation forcing the witness machinery does not do.

DEFERRED per the `.4b.13` DESIGN's explicit DEFER clause + the `.4b.12` family-B precedent + [[feedback_no_codebase_change_without_tool_backed_facts]]; the producer-admission + consumer-echo helpers are the correct first ingredients and can be re-landed as part of that capability slice (where they will move the metric). ## 2026-06-23 - PGEN-STORE-AWARE-GEN-0014 (STORE-AWARE-GEN.4b.8, GENERATOR-ONLY): store-aware collide-aware free-name diversity — SV cert UNKNOWN 38 → 37 (+1 witnessed: property_qualifier), zero newly-UNKNOWN

Generator-only; no parser/grammar/generated/release/schema change; SV row stays `Mostly Done` (closure-debt retirement). **Decisive A/B on the regen-lockstep build:** SV certificate-coverage `UNKNOWN 38 → 37`, witness `1250 → 1251`, `spf=0`, `proof_reverify_failures=0`, deterministic at seeds 0/7/42; the newly-witnessed rule is `property_qualifier` (`class\foo ;rand\foo_0 ;endclass`).

- **Tools-first WHY+WHERE (a witness-generator name collision).** `property_qualifier := random_qualifier` (`:4228`) and `variable_identifier := declaration_identifier` (`:5419`) are both UNGATED — not a store-gate cohort member. The reach context wraps the target in `class_declaration`, so the witness names the class with the canonical identifier `\foo` (emitting a `type_name` fact via `class_identifier`'s `@emit_fact`, `:965`) AND re-renders the SAME canonical `\foo` (the `@sample: "\\foo "` on `escaped_identifier`, `:356`) as the free `variable_identifier`. Since `\foo` is now a known type, PEG's `data_type_or_implicit := data_type | implicit_data_type` (`:1730`) tries `data_type` FIRST and greedily consumes `\foo` as the TYPE, dropping the mandatory `list_of_variable_decl_assignments` → REJECT. `PGEN_CERT_COVERAGE_DEBUG_PROBES`: forced `class\foo ;rand\foo ;endclass` `parsed=false`. `parseability_probe` A/B: `class\foo ;rand\foo ;endclass` REJECT `furthest_position=19` vs `class\foo ;rand\foo \bar ;endclass` (distinct variable name) PASS.
- **What landed (generator-only, the generation-side dual of the parser's type-vs-identifier disambiguation).** Two helpers in `stimuli_generator.rs`: `free_name_collides_gate_kind` (does a token already exist in the generation store under a fact kind some positive name-gate consumes?) and `diversify_free_name_avoiding_gate_collision` (on collision, append the smallest `_<n>` clearing both the gate-kind collision and active keyword exclusions, preserving leading/trailing layout so the escaped-identifier whitespace terminator survives). Hooked at the rule-level `@sample` literal-hint override in `generate_rule`. DETERMINISTIC and RNG-NEUTRAL (no re-roll), keyed on the grammar's OWN name-gate kinds (parser-agnostic, never a rule name).
- **Why the producer's own declaration is exempt (no special-casing).** A producer emits its `type_name` fact only AFTER its own render completes, so at the class-name render the store is empty (no collision); the variable renders later, when `\foo` is present (collision → diversified). The most-recent-fact read-back (`store_name_for_gate`) is therefore unaffected — this never diversifies the declaration a name-coordinated consumer must echo.

## 2026-06-23 - PGEN-STORE-AWARE-GEN-0011 (STORE-AWARE-GEN.4b.6, GENERATOR-ONLY): self-bootstrapping HOST-BRANCH producer selection — SV cert UNKNOWN 43 → 41 (+2 class-scope rules witnessed), zero newly-UNKNOWN

Landed the generator-only engine change pinned by `.4b.5`, on the most-tuned generation surface (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs`). No parser/grammar/generated/release/schema change; SV row stays `Mostly Done` (closure-debt retirement, not a row flip). **Decisive A/B on the regen-lockstep build:** SV certificate-coverage `UNKNOWN 43 → 41`, witness `1245 → 1247`, `spf=0`, deterministic at seeds 0/7/42.

- **Tools-first ROOT-CAUSE REFINEMENT (the first cut was a no-op).** `.4b.5` pinned "prefer a self-bootstrapping producer", and the first implementation checked the producer RULE's own body for a same-kind gate. The A/B was decisive that it did **nothing** (`UNKNOWN` stayed `43`, the forced sample byte-identical). Reading the grammar with the toolbox showed why: BOTH family=class producers reachable from the top-level site share the byte-identical body `type_identifier` (`declared_class_alias_identifier := type_identifier` `:5115`, `declared_forward_class_identifier := type_identifier` `:5119`) — a producer-BODY check cannot tell them apart. The non-bootstrapping-ness lives in the producer's **HOST BRANCH** of `type_declaration`: the alias sits in `kw_typedef class_type declared_class_alias_identifier …` (`:5146`), whose `class_type` **mandatory sibling** descends to a `has_fact(type_name,·)` gate; the forward sits in `kw_typedef kw_class declared_forward_class_identifier semi` (`:5152`), a clean `kw_class` literal. `parseability_probe` proved it: the alias prelude `typedef\foo \foo ;…` REJECTs `furthest_position=11`; the forward prelude `typedef class\foo ;…` PASSES; the real-class prelude `class\foo ;endclass…` PASSES.
- **What it does — two-pass HOST-PATH-aware producer selection.** `reach_path_renders_unsatisfiable_gate(hops)` + `offpath_siblings_gated_along_path(...)` walk the producer's reach-path hops (the `collect_rule_reference_sites` `node_path` encoding) and, at every Sequence crossed, test each MANDATORY off-path sibling with the existing `mandatory_node_gated` store-gate walk against an EMPTY available set — flagging the typedef-alias path (its `class_type` sibling is gated) and not the forward path. `compute_name_prelude` wraps its site/producer loops in `for prefer_clean in [true, false]`: PASS 1 skips any producer whose forced reach path is gated; PASS 2 restores the exact pre-4b.6 "first reachable" fallback, so a candidate is never dropped. For an already-witnessed target the chosen producer's path is necessarily clean, so PASS 1 selects the SAME producer — the change only promotes a clean producer where the pre-4b.6 path committed a gated one (and so never witnessed). The parser re-check stays the sole witness judge.
- **+2 class-scope rules witnessed:** `known_unscoped_class_scope_class_identifier`, `known_unscoped_class_scoped_call_class_identifier` (the 3B-ii pair). Remaining 3B: gate-not-mandatory-first (`extern_constraint_declaration*`, `constraint_set`) → `.4b.7`; target-own incompleteness (`property_qualifier`) → `.4b.8`; reach-routing 3C → `.4b.9`; SVA infix parse-bug + `no_path` out of scope.
- **Capability-gated / no-op for everyone else.** Keyed on `gen_name_gate` non-empty (only SystemVerilog declares positive name-gate predicates — 33; all 6 fully-certified grammars 0) ⇒ `compute_name_prelude` early-returns ⇒ byte-identical for predicate-free grammars; the count path (`compute_count_prelude`) is untouched ⇒ regex byte-identical.
- **No regression (oracle-cited).** ZERO newly-UNKNOWN (the new 41 is a script-verified strict SUBSET of the baseline 43 — `comm -13` empty; the only two rules that left are the addressed pair); regex byte-identical `fully_certified=true 198/198` at seeds 0/7/42; json (9/9) / vhdl (216/216) / svpp (74/74) / rtl_frontend (169) all `fully_certified=true` (rtl_const_expr `store_aware_gen=false` ⇒ path off, green in the lib suite); `cargo test --lib --features "generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run"` **764 passed / 0 failed** (+1 locking test `store_aware_gen_prefers_self_bootstrapping_host_branch`); `clippy_on_rust_change` source stage clean (zero findings in the changed code; the generated-`eq_op` errors pre-existing in `generated/*_parser.rs`). ## 2026-06-22 - PGEN-STORE-AWARE-GEN-0006 (STORE-AWARE-GEN.4b.2, GENERATOR-ONLY): name-coordinated declare-then-use witness prelude — SV cert UNKNOWN 56 → 46 (+10 store-gate cohort witnessed), zero newly-UNKNOWN

Landed the generator-only engine change pinned by `.4b.1` (the design half), on the most-tuned generation surface (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/stimuli_generator.rs`). No parser/grammar/generated/release/schema/ledger change; SV row stays `Mostly Done` (closure-debt retirement, not a row flip). **Decisive A/B on the regen-lockstep build:** SV certificate-coverage `UNKNOWN 56 → 46`, witness `1232 → 1242`, `spf=0`, deterministic at seeds 0/7/42.

- **What it does — declare-then-use name coordination.** The C2.2 semantic-prelude (which already hosts a fact PRODUCER upstream of a `fact_count_at_least(K,$ref)` count-gated rule for regex) is generalized to NAME-matching store gates (`has_fact(K,$ref)` / `fact_attribute_equals(K,$ref,declaration_family,V)`). To witness a use-site of a declared name (e.g. `checked_type_identifier`, `known_unscoped_covergroup_type_identifier`), the witness pass now: (1) declares a matching producer (a `declared_*` declaration whose `@emit_fact` registers a name) at one upstream quantifier iteration; (2) resolves the producer's `name: $body` to the rendered identifier so the store carries the REAL declared name; (3) forces the gated consumer's whole render to that live store name — so the re-parse sees declare-then-use and the `@predicate` passes. The certifying parser re-check stays the only witness judge (no false witness possible — a mis-coordination just fails to witness).
- **+10 store-gate cohort rules witnessed:** `checked_type_identifier`, `checked_nettype_identifier`, `known_unscoped_covergroup_type_identifier`, `known_unscoped_interface_class_type_identifier`, `known_unscoped_let_identifier`, `known_unscoped_parameter_identifier`, `known_unscoped_data_type_identifier`, `known_unscoped_class_scope_interface_class_identifier`, `known_unscoped_base_class_type_parameter_identifier`, `known_unscoped_block_class_type`. The deeper class-scope / class-member-context residual (`known_unscoped_class_scope_class_identifier`, `constraint_set`, `extern_constraint_declaration*`, the `class_scoped_*call*` family, `provisional_unscoped_block_class_type`) → follow-up `.4b.3`; the SVA infix parse-bug + `no_path` are out of scope per `.4b.1`.
- **Capability-gated / parser-agnostic / no-op for everyone else.** Keyed only on the predicates' presence (never a grammar name): json/vhdl/svpp/rtl_const_expr/rtl_frontend carry no store predicates ⇒ the whole path is off (byte-identical); regex's only `has_fact` is a comment and its emit name is a literal ⇒ byte-identical (re-verified `fully_certified=true` at seeds 0/7/42). A SELF-EMITTING producer (a rule that emits the kind it gates on — the `declared_forward_*`/`declared_*_alias` idiom) is excluded from the consumer cohort, so it is not forced to re-declare an already-declared name.
- **In-session regression caught + fixed tools-first.** The first cut regressed `declared_forward_class_identifier` (witnessed → UNKNOWN); `PGEN_CERT_COVERAGE_DEBUG_PROBES` named the cause (`typedef\foo \foo ;typedef class\foo ;` — the prelude declared `\foo`, then forced the self-emitting forward-class rule to RE-declare it → parse conflict). The self-emitting-producer exclusion fixed it; the final `46` is a strict SUBSET of the baseline `56` (script-verified ZERO newly-UNKNOWN — the M2a invariant).
- **No regression (oracle-cited).** cert seeds 0/7/42 `spf=0`; the 6 fully-certified grammars `fully_certified=true` (regex byte-identical); `cargo test --lib --features generated_parsers` **729 passed / 0 failed** (+3 new locking tests); `ast_shape_contract_gate` 18/18; `clippy_on_rust_change` source stage exits 0 (the 189 `eq_op` errors are all pre-existing in `generated/*_parser.rs`; zero new warnings in the changed source). ## 2026-06-22 - PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0120 (GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.12.5.8.3.1, PURE-DOCS CHECKPOINT): SVA SEQUENCE precedence-cascade implemented + parse-verified; coverage-regression root-caused; director decided KEEP CASCADE + FIX COVERAGE

Implementation checkpoint for the `.8.3` precedence-cascade (direction A). The §16 SEQUENCE cascade was implemented in the working tree and **parse-verified**, a coverage regression was root-caused tools-first, and the design fork it exposed was decided by the director. **PURE-DOCS ⇒ no committed code/grammar/generated/release/schema/ledger change** (the cascade lives uncommitted in the working tree); clippy not invoked; SV committed-baseline stays cert `UNKNOWN=56`; `systemverilog` LIVE row UNCHANGED (`Mostly Done`).

- **Cascade (parse-correct).** `sequence_expr` rewritten into the §16 Table 16-3 precedence cascade (`seq_or→seq_and→seq_intersect→seq_within→seq_throughout→seq_delay(##)→seq_unary`) using only proven idioms (`head tail tail*` chains with named tail rules, `-> $1` passthrough for bare operands, 2-element `[$v,$rest*]` arrays). Verified via the regenerated parser (`parseability_probe`): all previously-broken infix forms now parse (`a and/or/intersect/within b`, `a ##1 b`, `a ##1 b ##2 c`, `a or b and c`, `a intersect b within c`), all previously-working forms preserved (`a`, `a [*2]`, `first_match(a)`, `x throughout a`, `##1 a`), and the cert witnesses `kw_intersect`/`kw_within` with `spf=0`. **The released SVA infix-sequence parse bug is fixed at the grammar level.**
- **Coverage regression (open, root-caused).** Post-cascade cert (seed 0): `total=1300 witness=1234 UNKNOWN=65` — a regression from `56` because the cascade de-witnesses 9 `seq_unary` operand sub-rules (`boolean_abbrev` family / `sequence_abbrev` / `kw_first_match` / `sequence_instance`-related). WHY (tool-backed): **NOT depth** (`--max-depth` 24/32/40 all stay `65`; the witness-pass per-target budget that fully certifies `rtl_const_expr`'s 14-deep cascade is adequate) — it is a FORCING bug: with `PGEN_CERT_COVERAGE_DEBUG_PROBES=1`, the plannable pass reaches `seq_unary` via `seq_delay_expr`'s `delay_head` branch (`cycle_delay_range seq_unary`), `cycle_delay_range` greedily consumes the operand identifier, the following `seq_unary` expression comes out empty, and the forced `boolean_abbrev` lands as a bare `[*]` → invalid `## \foo [*]` → no re-parse → no witness. Forms PARSE; witness-REACH only. Not committable per "commit only improvements".
